title: Book Aimed at Young Movie-Makers Really Hits the Mark
text:
LEGO MAKE YOUR OWN MOVIE (by the editors of KLUTZ) is a how-to guide for stop-motion-movie-making, using LEGO minifigures and bricks. It’s aimed at young children, and it really hits the mark. I think that any child who is able to read the simple instructions should be able to make his/her own LEGO movies, and that even younger children can make stop-motion movies with adult help.

The book includes LEGO parts, background scenery, and basic scripts to get the reader started with a few simple movies, using animation apps that are loaded with cell phone cameras or that are readily available online as free downloads. My favorite feature of the book is the deck of “scene cards” that can be removed and photographed in sequence to test the performance of the reader’s chosen animation software.

If you perform this “scene card” test, you will master the basic photography skills needed, before you invest a lot of time setting up your stop-motion frames with actual LEGO pieces. This book isn’t just for kids, either—it’s a great starter book for anyone who’s interested in learning how to create his/her own LEGO movies.

title: OK as a beginner training drone or as a toy.
text:
UPDATE: My review below still stands as far as the performance & features, but I felt the need to mention my interaction with customer service at USA Toyz after posting this review. I had no plans to contact c/s about my dislike of the drone, but 4 hours after I posted the review, I was contacted by their c/s to express their concern over my dislike. Right up front in their first email to me they offered to upgrade me at n/c to a better model, so that I could have a good drone experience. I didn't even have to return the original model. I was flabbergasted. You just don't see this kind of customer service anymore now days. They were phenomenal & I love the upgraded model.
ORIGINAL REVIEW: This may be a little lengthy, but I hope it's helpful to undecideds. I've wanted to get into droning for awhile & in research found this model mentioned in several articles as the best model of 2017 for beginners. And it seemed to have the best Amazon rating among beginner drones. I didn't want to go straight into an expensive model & have it end up sitting on a shelf. My review is from the angle of someone seriously wanting to learn drone flying & using this to get thru the learning curve & then upgrading to a $600-$1000 drone if I master the functions & enjoy it
I've had 2 hours of total flying time which equals about 16 battery cycles or 16 flying sessions & using most of the features on it except the return home feature. When it arrived, I was shocked at how light & flimsy it was & thought it would fall apart quickly. But as others have mentioned, that's a good thing. The plastic guard rings are very flexible, more so than the blades. They seem to be just right for absorbing the shock of a crash, but the blades are just stiff enough to maintain shape & not permanently kink or bend like real soft plastic. I've crash landed at least 30 times, mostly in field grass, with a few times on a gravel drive or in bushy scrub trees with no damage so far except a few minor scratches. It even got muddy on one wet morning crash, but cleaned up easily. This lightness allows for maximum battery efficiency, but it has a downside. A light breeze (7-9 mph) can pull the drone away from you, especially in the slower reacting beginner mode, which I used for the first 7 sessions. As a result, I lost the drone twice in tall scrub brush that was almost impenetrable. I literally watched it slip away & could not bring it back at about 50 ft in the air where the breeze is a little stronger than at ground level. Always remember the winds are faster when you get much above ground level.
The stability is not that great but probably as expected for this price range, without the stabilizing features of the more expensive ones. I shot video most of the flying time & it came out quite jerky. There's also an annoying horizontal wave in all the videos that looks like a heat wave, but it wasn't hot when shooting. In video playback, the noise of the motors & blades is horrendous, so audio is useless & you'll want to mute it. Also the camera lens is fixed, so there is no independent movement of the camera with a gimbal that would allow you to move the camera up/down or left/right. The videos from this drone are not of much use because of the very jerky motion & unsteadiness of the light drone in the breeze. I might be able to improve this a little, with more practice, but not enough to produce an enjoyable video I would want to show someone else. I'm sure the videos shown in their advertising were taken by a top notch drone flyer in a dead calm setting.
Being a newbie, I was disappointed in the short battery life of each flying session, about 7 minutes tops.
The toggle controls are very sensitive & I find it difficult to maintain a certain altitude. It wants to climb much higher with just a touch of the toggle or drop to the ground. The flip feature is very fast. If you aren't watching closely, you'll miss it.
The response from tilting left or right, forward or backward, can be immediate or very slow, depending on a difference of only 2-4 mph breeze. So you need to be in a wide open area so the response time won't cause you any trouble. You could shoot downwind 100 yards in 5 seconds, but take 30 seconds to get it back upwind.
The total travel distance away from you & altitude attainable is very limited compared to the more expensive models.
You'll want more than the 2 included batteries if you want to spend an hour or two flying, since the battery recharge time is lengthy.
Instruction manual was written by someone in China with a very poor grasp of English grammar, which makes some instructions difficult to understand.

OVERALL: It's an ok drone & probably one of the best for learning the basics of drone flying. But I'm disappointed in the video quality, instability, & short run time. I'm not thrilled with this drone, but I'm not completely dissatisfied with it either. I plan to continue honing my flying skills with this drone & eventually upgrade to a true quality drone with good video features, stability control, live video feed, & extended range capabilities.

title: nice figure but not with certain flaws
text:
Bandai once again surprise everyone in there D-arts line by bringing another Megaman but not just any megaman but THE original Megaman. Megaman comes with some accessories that 2 of which are awesome to have:

- set of open hands and fist(one fist is already install in the figure).
- an extra Mega Buster meant to be use for his right arm (he already has a left one install in the figure).
- a left arm.
- a mega buster peg hole for attaching effect shots parts.
- a effect shots parts. (the triple small bullets like the ones that d-arts MMX figures would have but a bit smaller)
- 3 face parts: normal(already install in the figure angry and angry screaming.
- 1 mettaur.
- 1 Rush (megaman's dog companion.

This figure is nice and well accurate also really good articulated although a bit restrictive in contrast to the d-arts MMX figures in certain areas, more specifically his upper torso has practically a little to no articulation, however his waist articulation makes up for it. His feet doesn't extend as much as his d-arts MMX counterparts but it has some level of articulation. His shoulders is also another point that feels restricted but it still has good range of motion. Some might find his size to be small but in reality he is in scale to the D-arts Megaman X since X is much more taller than Classic Megaman, however to compensate for classic Megaman been shorter than the regular D-arts MMX, Bandai decided to release with this figure to more iconic characters with it. The first one been Rush, megaman's dog companion, his well articulated has swivels movement on the upper part of his legs while it has ball joints on his kness and ankles, his tail is on a ball joint as well his head and neck. the second one been the Mettaur one of the most iconic classic enemies of the classic megaman series if not in all megaman series, his just a simple figurine which it has not articulation, however it has a gimmick that you can take off his hat and put on a flat surface to make it look like its hiding just like they do in the game (nice touch). Now some of you might be thinking why Megaman comes with a second Mega buster, well the reason to this is because the second mega buster is meant for his right arm because of a specific design the buster has and that is the yellow bar thing. 1 Mega buster would not be able to suffice to do the job for both arms so it needs to be 2 mega buster, also it does a reference to a game that was for the PS1 (i think) that never got to the U.S. called Super Adventure Rockman where he uses 2 Mega Buster at the same time.

Now as a nice figure it is, it has a major flaw which is the joint of the upper part of his leg. My first figure that i order from Amazon came with the right leg broken off from its connection which i was able to see that it is really small and not well thought out by Bandai when designing it. When i tried to move the ball joint that was stuck in the leg it didn't move at all which it made me believe that it was really stiff and possible it broke during packaging of the figure in the factory. I had to send it back and Amazon send me a replacement (really fast i might add "thumbs up")which i got it today. For my surprise i was right, my second figure confirms me that the figures upper right leg joint movement is extremely stiff to the point it wouldn't budge and you might break it off. his left leg seems to do fine but i could feel that it was becoming stiff overtime. so what i had to do to my second megaman figure is to put it in hot water, pop the legs off from its ball joint very carefully. I notice some extra residua of plastic on the ball joints so i use a fine sandpaper to clean it off, then i added a little bit of a multipurpose lubricant to the connector point where the ball joint would be in and done, the leg joints of my megaman now feels much better and not so stiff, now its fun to play with and not worried about his leg joint breaking off anytime soon. Perhaps it might been bad luck for me of getting some bad ones i guess or Amazon has a batch of defectives, im not sure, all i know is just be careful on the purchase of this figure.

-Pros-
- Great level of detail.
- In scale with the D-arts MMX figures. (MM been smaller than MMX)
- It comes with his dog Rush and the enemy Mettaur.
- It brings a second mega buster for his right arm.
- has good articulation
- Packaging is nice looking.

-Cons-
- The figure is smaller than those of the d-arts MMX figures.(this might turn some people down)
- Rush does not transform or has any accessories to make him into the iconic flying Rush Jet.
- Mettaur has no articulation.
- no extra Mega Buster peg hole. (it comes with only one)
- Articulation is somewhat restricted in certain areas in comparison to the d-arts MMX figures (one of which his upper torso practically has no movement but depends on his waist joint to do so).
- upper legs movement are way to stiff and has the possibility of breaking the joint. (more noticeable on his right leg)

-overall-
It is a nice figure, heck I think its THE best classic Megaman figure rendition today, but it has some flaws, one been major as his upper joint of his leg might break off. I cannot recommend this figure for everyone unless you're a true Megaman fan. However if you do buy it, be advice about his legs problem and try to avoid by moving it to much or try fixing it yourself just like i did.

title: The love-child of Cribbage and Snakes & Ladders
text:
Cribbage had a one night stand with Snakes & Ladders, and Crib Wars is the secret love child that resulted. The basic game-play is like regular Cribbage, but you play on a much larger 363 hole board that has traps and shortcuts, similar to Snakes & Ladders.

The special locations on the board include:
- Red Skip: if you peg or land on this red location, you immediately advance 20 spaces to the matching red location.
- Green Advance: if you peg or land on this green location, you take a shortcut path that effectively saves you 30-60 pegholes.
- Blue Penalty Box: If you peg or land on this blue location, you fold your hand and go back 20 pegholes while your opponent goes forward pegholes.
- Blue Time Trap: If you peg or land on this blue location, you must follow the blue path which leads backwards and effectively requires another 30 pegholes

The main impact on the game-play is three-fold:
1. More variety: Crib Wars does present players with new tactical choices, e.g. to peg in a way so as to avoid or to land on certain spots. Sometimes you *don't* want to score points due to your board situation! Some people will enjoy this change up from regular Cribbage.
2. More luck: Even the most skilled players will find it quite a challenge to land on or avoid certain pegholes, and often getting the bonuses or penalties comes down to luck. To keep this from being too frustrating, some players recommend playing with a house rule that each time trap or penalty area only counts once at most against each player - otherwise you could find yourself in an almost endless loop.
3. More time: Expect a long game of about 2 hours, especially if you find yourself stuck in the same Time Trap multiple times!

For most Cribbage fans, this is just a novelty item that you'll be done with after playing it a couple of times at most. It is really for the serious Cribbage player, who likes the challenge of a marathon session and doesn't mind some new tactical twists as well as some new random elements. So while hardcore Cribbage players might enjoy this, the average player will likely consider Crib Wars to be a Cribbage "death match" and prefer to just play a series of several regular Cribbage games instead. Crib Wars is really geared to those who enjoy Cribbage a lot and are looking for a new challenge, so if you meet those criteria, you might want to give this a look. - EndersGame @ BGG

title: Maybe more fun for the adults!
text:
This car takes a 9 volt battery in the control and 3 AAA batteries in the car. Getting the 9v into the battery compartment is easy...but the 3 AAA's, not so much. You access the battery port through the top of the car, you need a long, tiny phillip's screwdriver, and once you get the top cover off, there is an additional cover to remove before you can actually access the battery compartment.

Seems a little overpriced and the tires are hard plastic, would be nice if they were made from a different material.

The tires have a lot of wheel spin, probably due to the hard plastic, and this could be why battery life is rather short, the car drives nicely on carpet, hard wood floors not so much. Grass is ok but gravel is a lot of fun...creates entertainment while it catapults across the yard!

We haven't tried this in the lake yet....

The car is rather loud, but the look is pretty awesome, scares the cats and dog half out of their minds.

Fun once you get used to the controls and could provide endless hours of fun but the batteries don't last long at all.....kept my 18 year old son entertained for quite some time! The controls take a bit of time to get used to...you need to push both controls to go forward or backward...I can see little kids getting a bit frustrated while they learn the technique...but in the end I think they'd have fun.

Priced a bit on the high side, but at least it provides fun and entertainment...for ALL ages!

title: Broke after 9 months; warranty not honored
text:
Our daughter enjoyed this speaker very much while it worked. The sound is respectable for the size, and hey, it's a cute panda!

Unfortunately, after only nine months, the audio input plug no longer fit into any MP3 player or computer headphone jack. It appears that the metal banding on the plug failed from inserting it into input devices a few times each week, and it gradually "flared" until it was no longer usable. The headphones that came with her audio device are still working great, so it is definitely a problem with this plug, not the audio player.

We were grateful for the 3-year warranty, and contacted the company for information on a repair or replacement. Unfortunately, they refused to honor their warranty, as the warranty only covers defects in manufacturing and not damages. (I'm not sure what kind of manufacturing defect does not cause damage, but whatever.)

I'm going to try a little Dremel magic and see if I can get things working again, but am disappointed at the lack of support the company provides for their product. I hope your experience is better.

title: Do you know EVERYTHING about Doctor Who yet?
text: I did not realize this when I originally put it on my wish list, so I will emphasize this: Although this is an officially branded Trivial Pursuit game, it is not the traditional complete board game. It is a sort of condensed version, with only the cards and a die that you use to select the question's category; these come in a large plastic TARDIS-blue wedge. It is great for travel, and you can use the cards in place (or mixed into) the regular game set if you want. One of the category colors is purple, which we substitute for brown from the original when using the pies. The questions cover ALL of Doctor Who history, so be prepared to either know a LOT about DW, or quickly learn. I would like to someday see a full game-board with Doctor Who imagery all over it. I would definitely recommend it for the more extreme Doctor Who fans.

title: first telescope
text: My 6yo had been begging for a telescope since his teacher mentioned the word astronomy and taught the class about ancient stargazers.  Luckily, we were chosen to review this telescope and my son got straight to work trying to predict the future from the stars.  Out of the box he was able to assemble all the pieces and figure out all the attachments with just a bit of reading help from his older siblings.  As recommended  in the instruction guide, it was distorted through the window so we decided to save it for a clear night outdoors.  The legs fold flat for travel so he stored it in a little drawstring backpack until he had a chance to use it outdoors.  My kids were able to see the moon and some stars although in the city with all the tall buildings it was kind of hard to see much.  The activity journal comes with some suggested activities so we did look at some buildings and trees and tried different eyepieces.  My son also enjoyed looking at the phases of the moon even though we didn't always have a chance to use it outdoors during all the phases.  We forgot the telescope when we went camping but my son was able to try a real telescope and was really impressed by what he saw.  This telescope is more of a toy and an introduction to telescopes.  It currently has found a place in our toybox more for pretend play.

These cars are an excellent way to keep a child busy and entertained for a half hour or so. As an added bonus, they will also get to use their own screwdriver to put the pieces together. They will need help getting the screws started and tightening them at the end. My kindergartener was most excited about assembling these kits, so I let him go for it on the first one before painting. It still turned out looking very good, a few paint splotches here and there but who cares. On the second car, he wanted to try painting it first. The paint dried pretty quickly so by the time he was done painting, he could put some pieces together. I evened out some of the painting, got the screws started, and tightened them up, but he did most of the work independently. I didn’t help with the instructions but he had no problems. My youngster gets a lot of joy out of feeling independent so this was awesome for him.

They are not heirlooms, but they are quite nice wood cars. When I was a kid, my dad and I put together a few model car kits that required precision gluing little pieces together and applying decals. These are not those, children do not need to have a lot of patience to get these looking good. And you can even play with them after, not like the ‘57 Chevy model sitting on a shelf at my dad’s house. There were a few issues on some pieces that weren’t drilled quite deep enough so those pieces were loose. A little wood glue fixed that but I would rather they were drilled right. I also would have liked more paint, especially red. There is juuust enough to paint one full car if the child wants all the pieces the same color, so if they put 2 palettes with the same colors rather than two different palettes that would have been better. Other than those minor issues, this was an excellent craft and really fun project. I admit I enjoyed it too.

title: Clever Design, AI needs work
text:
This chess computer purports to be able to determine the level of an opponent after a few moves. If so it overrates me. I just lost a game to it in "Friendly Mode" by a mate by two pawns and a knight after 21 moves! The program that it is based on seems to have many scenarios memorized and these get used even when it should be playing a weak player. According to the manual it gets "smarter" as your chess improves. If so it will be very difficult to beat it since its underlying chess engine is extremely powerful. It is clearly a very good chess player. But its AI is not very good. I would rather be able to choose the level of play rather than let the computer decide after a few moves (and it seems to consistently decide incorrectly in my case). I am pretty good at chess puzzles (low 1600's on chesspuzzle.com) and I know a few opening moves, but my middle game needs work. I would guess that I am in the 1300 ballpark, but this computer makes me feel much lower than that. I have been reading books, but this computer is not a good way of practicing the ideas suggested. I understand that it can be dumbed down manually by overriding its choice of move but I don't think that chess is interesting when playing against oneself.
To sum up, it has 5 star hardware, a 5 star chess engine and 2 star AI which makes it frustrating.
Update: I have suddenly started to beat it. Perhaps it it teaching me to play chess.

title: Nice for display purposes, but not easy to assemble
text:
I needed some small anatomical models for my business. These did the trick, but they were not easy to put together! The heart and the torso were relatively straight forward. The skeleton was awkward, but I managed it. The brain was nearly impossible! I am a licensed health professional, skilled in anatomy and I could not for the life of me figure out the brain. I had to sit down with all the pieces in front of me and the instructions (which are really just diagrams) and put this thing together piece by piece, constantly checking for placement and alignment. I think it took me 20 minutes or more to get it together!
The package says this is for age 8 and up. Not only were they challenging to put together, but there are small pieces that could be hazardous. I realize an 8-year-old usually knows not to put small pieces in their mouths, but these are not something I would give to an 8-year-old. Besides, it's clear that these are for learning purposes because they have hinges and removal parts so you can see the insides. BUT, they don't assemble/disassemble easily and sometimes the hinged items just fall off.

title: Better than I expected!
text:
I recently purchased a couple of Ultra-Pro Deck Boxes from a large Big Box retailer, and I was happy with them for storing my extra cards. I wanted something that really stood out, and was durable, this absolutely fits the bill! The magnet is strong enough to keep the sleeved (Dragon Shield) cards in the box when traveling but not so much as to keep closed when opening with one hand.

-Material
The logo is debossed (pressed in) and looks like it will stay detailed for a while, the material is a faux leather (I would have happily paid triple for real leather) and doesn't have a distracting odor like I find with most "pleather" products. The stitching is tight, and clean and it looks to be able to withstand multiple trips in a backpack to shops. The inner box is lined with a velvet-like material and seems to do a good job as a small cushion for protecting cards as there is a lot of extra room for them.

-Usability
To each his own... I baby my cards, and my only complaint (not worth a star) is the fact that there is easily an inch or two with a full 60-card sleeved deck on the side. I've tried adding a 15-card sideboard, but it only lessens the gap, There is a lot of room for cards to bounce around during traveling.

-Bottom Line
If you are looking for an upgrade to the standard $4 Deck Box, invest in this, it is well built, looks awesome, and what better way to show your colors!

Within the last few months, he had several opportunities to try the adult version of Tangoes, or Tangrams, at a friend's house, which has more pieces than Jr (which has 7) and no shape outlines and he had trouble with it. title: Lovely bank for a little girl
text:
This is a very pretty carriage bank that is ideal for a little girl's bedroom. The shape of the carriage reminds me of a pumpkin which makes me think this is Cinderella's coach. The detailing on this bank is nicely done. There are a few areas where I feel like the lines of the paint could be a bit better, but overall it's a beautiful bank. I have three daughters ranging in age from 4 1/2 up to 14 and all three of them thought it was quite a nice bank, and each of them asked if it was for their baby sister who hasn't yet made her arrival.
I like that the slot for the bank is on the wider side so younger children won't have an incredible amount of difficulty in adding coins to the bank. The stopper on the bottom of the bank is easy to pop out and put back in place.
The bottom of the bank's wheels are a bit rough, so I'd strongly suggest adding felt pads to the bottom to prevent the bank from scratching furniture.
Because this is a ceramic bank you'll want to make sure that you put this in a safe place where little ones won't break it.
Overall it's a lovely bank for a sweet little princess. I think for the price point some protective feet should have been placed on the bottom of the bank to keep it from causing scratching on furniture, even the little banks that cost a small fraction of this price at Target come with protective pads on the bottoms of the banks.

title: How to attach
text:
The instructions were a blurry mess that I couldn't read. So instead I studied the photos on the amazon page for this product. Here's how I attached it.

(1) Attach a carabiner to the bottom (uncoated) chain link, and attach the rings to this carabiner.

(2) Attach a second carabiner to the (coated) next adjacent chain link, and attach the trapeze to this carabiner.

Once assembled it does look kind of janky, seeing the trapeze hanging off one chain-link and the bars off another. I went back and looked at rival products on amazon and the others look more elegant because their rings attach to the bottom of the trapeze. I wonder why the makers of this product suggest to use two separate carabiners? Why don't they tell you to hang the rings off the same carabiner that holds the trapeze? Is it because the carabiner is too flimsy? Why didn't they pick a stronger carabiner? Is it because a stronger carabiner wouldn't fit inside the chain links? I don't know.

Anyway, I've only assembled the thing, not yet given it to my kids to play with. I'll report back in a couple of weeks to see how it turned out in practice.

title: Excellent for outdoor AND indoor use!
text:
I have owned a bounce house before this one and, after some abuse, it died and could not be repaired. It was also pretty loud.

This bounce house, however, is very well made (but it does come with some good-sized vinyl patches, just in case) and the noise level from the fan is actually quite tolerable. Your kids might be noisier! :) We even set this up in our living room, which is pretty roomy but has ceilings of normal height, and were happy to see it fit just fine. Our three kids (ages 5, 9, and 12) absolutely love it and the 300 lb capacity gives me peace of mind that they can jump to their heart's content. The colorful balls are a nice touch for the kids, as well; I definitely recommend adding them. I like to fill the ball "hamper" up, climb up on a stool, and shower the kids with the balls from above while they are playing around inside. It's great fun for us all.

An earlier reviewer compared the clean-up process to rolling up a sleeping bag. That's basically right. Untie the smaller tube, fold the deflated bounce house in half two or three times, step on it to get more of the air out, and start rolling it up like a sleeping bag. The bounce house and the blower really do fit well in the included bag.

This was a Christmas present, so we haven't used it outside yet. But, as the weather improves, we are looking forward to putting it out on our lawn in the back yard and inviting some of the neighborhood kids over. It is sure to be a big hit.

title: Serve its purposes but not the best puzzle around
text:
I bought this product as I like to a) challenge myself and b) hang the finished product up on to the wall. Amazon is always reliable so I'm just going to focus on the product itself

What I like about it:
_ Challenging: Yes it is challenging (8/10) since you only have gray-scale. But I think that is the point.
_ Color difference: What you see is 80% what you get, which is decent. I have bought other puzzles whose yellow turned out to be orange, or blue turned out to be purple. The "shade of gray" here is pretty close to what I saw on the label, so it's good
_ Cheap

What I do not like about it:
_ No glue: My previous puzzles all either come with a glue pack or do not require glue at all. Therefore it's a shame that a well-known brand such as Ravensburger does not have one inside (or at least inform customer about it)
_ Poor quality:
+ Some of the paper edges are tearing apart.
+ The backing of the puzzle is blue and blue dust is EVERYWHERE. My hands become dirty just by sorting the pieces. Needless to say, you have to be careful not to breath in any of that stuff.
+ Some pieces are still not fully separated from one another. It helps the solving process, but no that's not good quality
_ No replacement policy

As I said above, the puzzle serves its purposes. Quality is not of premium one. I should have just stayed with Pintoo as their plastic puzzles are much much better than this low quality, paper one.

title: Fundamentally flawed game design
text:
I wanted to like this game, I really did, but it didn't take long to see the fundamental flaw in the game. Before I point that out, let me explain a bit about the rules. Each person chooses a character, and each character has a different goal or objective in order to win the game. There are two sets of cards: your villain cards which you play to achieve your goal, and fate cards, which other players play to try to thwart you. Sound fun, right? Only until you realize that the fate cards aren't really worth playing (I won't bother you with the long explanation why). This means it's not really a group game, but rather each person is basically playing by themselves. In fact, you could even play one player if you wanted to, but where's the fun in that?

All in all, it's more of a game of chance than of strategy. If you get the right villain cards at the right time, then you can move towards your goal. If not, it can be difficult to get the cards you need. Allow me to give an example: Jaffar. For Jaffar to win, you need to get the Genie, but to get the Genie, you need to play the Lamp card, but to play the Lamp card, you need the Scarab card. There's a bit more to it than that, but suffice it to say, you need these two cards to even begin towards you objective, and it's all a matter of luck if you find them at the right time or in the right order. I played a game where I got the Lamp card right away, but the Scarab card, as it turned out, was near the bottom of the deck. To get there, you have to draw more cards, but to draw more cards you need to either play cards or land on a space that allows discards. Playing cards is easier said than done, and many cards cannot be played without the addition of other cards. Basically, you can easily get stuck with cards that you cannot play. So, your only option is to use the discard action, which is only available every other turn. Stupid design, and frustrating to say the least.

Hopefully you see now the design flaw. It makes me wonder, did the game designers not test the game? No focus groups? Nothing? I really hope the game designers read this and confess to their sins! Please don't waste your money on this. If you want t good Disney game, try Disney Codenames or Disney Pictopia.

title: Great for visual learners
text: My son is hard of hearing and really struggles when people orally explain complicated rules to him.  My uncle sent us this chess set and it has been fantastic... It is so visually based and easy to understand.  It took away all the drama of learning a new game.  Both my 7 yo and 4 yo learned the basics within 2 days. If you want them to understand strategy, I suggest some heavy coaching to help them look at all their options... But after only a short time doing this (a few days!) my kids are able to figure things out themselves and they are able to anticipate their opponent's moves.  Be advised that levels 1, 2 and 3 are not pure chess and the stretegy is very different.  This is a great way to introduce the basics in a stepwise fashion, and it makes it different but enjoyable for experienced chess players who are teaching new players.  So impressed with this set. I love watching my kids play and think about their moves.

title: Great Marble Fun - Ages 8(?) AND UPPP!
text:
[[VIDEOID:83462ca03cf60cd6cd5f6641f199d0ad]] This is an awesome set of 200 colorful sturdy plastic pieces for building a mega marble run maze. There are SO many fun and interesting components to this; you can follow the “included” directions & build the [shown] mega maze, or use your imagination to create your own maze. Either way it is great entertainment [away from screens!!] for everyone involved!

There are lots of different paths that can be built with this, several different ball drop-in areas, and different marble collection areas. It also comes with “3” different types of marbles: glass, plastic, and Glo-in-the dark, which have different speeds and sounds. So many pieces to be creative with!!

I’m a bit confused as it states Ages 8+ on website, & on a shipping sticker, but my box says Age 3+? I would not recommend this set for a 3y/o, as there are too many small pieces & tiny marbles to worry about. But, we are a household that LOVES a good marble run at ANY AGE (much older than 8y/o LOL!)—so we had to give this a try!! And it did not disappoint.

That is not to say there haven’t been a couple complaints about the way a few pieces line up—it’s not “perfect”—but lots of fun has been had with it. Even Grandma got in on the fun when she came over! We did have to hide the marbles, as our cats would steal them from the collection pit and run off with them, lol!! It’s also a very BIG set, so make sure you have space, as ours got to be around 2.5’H x 2’W (give or take!). It a good value!

text:
[[VIDEOID:3714bdea02ef565dde57b5a327c1ddb]] Came well packaged, with just the handle unassembled. My 3yo got a kick out of helping me “build” the bubble machine.

We tried both plugged in and battery and it worked perfectly both ways. We stuck with the batteries though for mobility.

TILT WARNING WITH BATTERY - the batteries really weigh down the back half of the unit so when you pick it up by the handle, it tilts back quite a lot. The bubble solution could leak into the unit.

Other than that, I couldn’t want much more out of a bubble machine. It is sturdy and won’t topple in a bit of wind.

2oz of solution lasted 5 minutes on level 2. On level 1, the 2oz lasted much longer and the kids didn’t complain about the quantity of bubbles. I can’t say yet how long the batteries last.

title: This terrarium takes lots of time and effort!
text: While this product is a good introduction into the world of growing carnivorous plants. I HIGHLY recommend you do your research and know what your getting yourself or your children into. Carnivorous plants take quite a lot to grow and care for and its recommend you research the three plants included in this kit. Some tips as well, pitcher plants need to cold stratify before germination. Skip the dirt included in the kit and just used a damp paper towel. Put it into a Zip lock bag and leave it in your fridge for 4-5 weeks. Your seed will not grow if you dont do this. Another thing, the substrate that this kit comes with is very poor quality. I recommend a base of orchid bark growing medium at the bottom of the terrarium(about and inch and a half) and the rest sphagnum peat moss (up to a ¼ inch from the rim) for the best growing medium. Both of those can be found commonly at garden and hardware stores. This kit takes time, so dont be discouraged if nothing sprouts in the first month. If you or your children are looking to get into carnivorous plants, this is a good gateway but is slow to show results.

title: SO MUCH FUN!
text:
This is my first R/C Helicopter. While I am a woefully poor pilot, I started getting the hang of it after about 20 minutes and had a blast doing so.

In the box is the Quadcopter (actually larger than I expected), a full set of replacement blades, a remote (4 AAA batteries are included), the Quadcopter battery pack and USB charger. This is absolutely everything you need to operate the Ominus right out of the box. It's packaged well and I had no issues with shipping damage.

Operation is very tricky, as I assume it is for all R/C copters. It takes a little extra dexterity to be able to fine tune and adjust while flying. This seems to be the appeal of the R/C Copter hobby. It's very rewarding to expertly pilot the tiny copter, navigating around your home. Operating time averages 15 minutes on a single charge (this seems to be the average across most brands) and recharging takes about half an hour.

It's pretty loud, but no more so than I would expect any copter to be. The blades hurt when they hit you or others. Children should be supervised while operatin any R/C Copter, especially around other people or animals. The blades do have a safety feature that causes them to stop when they meet any resistance, but it's still probably possible to take out an eye (human or pet) if the right circumstances occur. Better safe than sorry. Again, this is all R/C Copters, not just the Ominus.

It's surprisingly durable. As I stated, I'm a crappy pilot. I spent the first 20 minutes smashing into everything within ten feet of me. The Ominus, had no issues and I didn't break any blades. Copters apparently get "drift" from time to time. This is when something gets decalibrated to an extent and when hovering it will drift one way or the other. The ominus has buttons on the controller that allow you to adjust and eliminate the drift. They work very well and the improvement was immediate.

Outside flying isn't really an option with the Ominus or most small copters. The air drafts are just too much for it. If it's a particularly windless day, you can probably get away with it, but don't count on using this outside too often.

Lastly, the Ominus can do flips. This is accomplished by activating the flip button and moving one way or the other. I have not been able to succesfully execute a flip, but only tried twice. This is not do to any shortcomings of the Copter itself, it's purely user error. It's a pretty cool feature and I look forward to being able to pull it off eventually.

I'm having a blast with this Quadcopter and it's definitely got me hooked on R/C copters in general. If you or a child is looking into getting an R/C Copter, go with the Ominus, you won't be disappointed!

title: Awesome Kite!
text:
Never knew about parafoil kites as I've always grown up with the typical diamond or delta kite with fiberglass poles.
This kite is made of a nylon material and uses NO POLES. You do need at least 10mph wind for it to fly, but it's easy as hold it, let the air holes fill up with air (takes 2 seconds), and let go while slowly releasing the string. I also suggest buying a spool for about $6 which makes kite flying a lot easier and more fun than having to unravel the free string spool/holder that comes with it and any entry level kite. Kite is easy enough for a 3 year old to fly. Comes with a carrying sack that you can simply fold or stuff the kite into.

title: Fun Bath Toy
text:
Bath time is always a big hit in our house, and now that we have this bath toy setup the kids love it even more. I think the best part is how many different combinations you can setup and test out. Each of the large pieces has four separate connection spots that you can control the flow of water at. You can turn outer ring to fully open, close, or even leave it partly open to control the water flow.

There are many wonderful STEM experiences from this set, from the engineering of the setup to the problem solving and testing of each idea. There were a few times the kids tried something and realized it was not working as expected. They spent another five minutes going through and checking that each connection was set right, the water could flow where they wanted it, and even tested out variations of angles to help direct the water to the path that they wanted.

If you have a kid who likes to experiment with water, this is a great toy to get for the bath. If you have two kids, I highly recommend getting two sets, as this set does not have enough parts to divide between two kids and still allow for great experimentation.

Its sturdy enough, I never had any problems with leaks, and the backrest is really a neck saver... not to mention the cup holders, which rock. I had a plain yellow inner tube before I got the River Run and the River Run beats it by a long shot.

title: Ultimate rip-off
text:
Whoever thinks that this is a cool toy or worth the money must be uber rich, spoilt brats. For $300 you get a car that will make you smile for 2 minutes, but the painful remorse of spending $300 on this will last you a lot longer. For all that money, you get a really, really poorly designed control interface, which basically means that you'll just want to put it on the shelf and look at it, and when your friends come, tell them how you had $300 that you could have spent so much more meaningfully, but you went and bought this ultimate rip off of a car that no one can drive.

If you can, test drive it. Just try to make it get out of a corner. Try to back it up. Try to make it come to you. Just anything. I kid you not. This is so poorly designed an experience, that you wonder how in the world's order does it fit in that a company can so blatantly put this product on the market and manage to get so many people to write about it in glowing words.

Don't have enough swear words for the people who designed this car and then convinced all the people to write about it so glowingly that I got suckered into buying it. Get a $20 RC car and you'll not only have more fun, but if you break it 15 times over, you can buy it again and again, and still not spend as much as you would on this car.

title: Hot wheels AND monster trucks?!?!? Yes!!!
text:
I’m quite surprised at how big this thing is! That’s not a bad thing I just didn’t expect it to be quite so long/big. My father takes my kids and my sisters kids to a monster jam show at least once a year. So they all really love anything that has to do wi Th monster trucks. And they have always loved Hot wheels, even my girls love them both. So when I saw that they had made a Hot wheels And monster trucks scorpion raceway set I was excited!

Set up was ok, basically like setting up any other hot wheels tracks it takes a few minutes and is pretty easy. It’s a lot longer/larger than i thought it would be. I was pumped it has a booster that can boost both the cars and the monster trucks. Though I will say the cars go great from the booster but the monster trucks not so much. They mostly never make it across the scorpion gap,,,but the kids like that so no biggie. There’s a few ways you can go on this track. You can either go in full circles or you can go right at the scorpion from the other track and attempt to “defeat” him. Be aware that the booster takes 4 D batteries! We had to run out to our local store to get them after I set it up. I really should start keeping those around!

Overall the kids really like this track. We already own many of the monster jam trucks and they enjoyed seeing if any of them would make the jump over the scorpion. The track feels solid, at least as solid at hot wheels tracks get. Definitely recommend for anyone with kids that like hot wheels and monster trucks!

title: Saved one of the best for last!
text:
General Rattlor was the only figure missing from my 200X Masters collection. I never owned the original, so there was no nostalgia compelling me to track him down. And that's what was required, a hunt, given that I never once saw this figure in stores when originally released at the end of the 200X line. As time passed, I even overlooked his absence from my collection; my interest was focused on the newer Classics line. But then Mattel released the character as a Classics figure and, nice as that one is, I was reminded how much I loved the 200X designs. Rather than purchase a Classics Rattlor, I decided it was time to find the previous release.

Wow! This is really one of the best figures from the 200X line. He's nearly as tall as a Classics figure, has a nice arc in the action feature that allows his neck to extend and his head to thrust forward, has a hinged upper jaw, and has an actual rattle built into his tail! This just reminds me what a shame it was that the line didn't move forward after the introduction of the snake men. This figure is a perfect example of the best the line had to offer.

title: Really cool drone, now I have a free controllable replacement.
text:
I just received a brand new HS170. The right front motor is bad. I does not spin up with the other motors. It starts late and makes it uncontrollable. I did just contact Holy Stone and they said they would give me a new motor which I can install myself. OK, I've seen the video and I can do that easily enough. But I will have to wait until this happens and I can fly it properly. Then I will edit this review.

Edit: I found out it wasn't the motor. I decided to try zeroing the gyros and and it works. But I do find it difficult to control. It can't keep a steady height. As soon as I move it any direction (only a little bit too) it suddenly wants to rise too fast, and when I back off it sinks too fast. I am indoors right now and I have seen videos of it indoors but I sure can't get smooth control over it. I found I had to play with the trim a lot too to try to keep it from drifting too much. I suppose I'll have better luck outdoors without the walls or ceiling to hit, but it still is difficult to control.

Edit: Holy Stone is trying to help me out so far. But I find this drone is pretty uncontrollable. As soon as I give it a directional command (right stick) it just starts climbing too, outdoors it must have went over 30 feet high. So I lower the throttle slowly to bring it down and then when it finally starts descending it comes down quickly and I have to raise the throttle back up so it doesn't fall to the ground. I was really looking forward to having fun with this drone but it's an effort to just try to get it do fly around in any direction. It can't keep a steady altitude. Sure , I know it doesn't have altitude control but it shouldn't climb or descend like crazy when I just try to make it go right/left/fwd/back. Even just moving the Yaw control it starts to descend.

Edit: Holy Stone is giving me another HS170 at no cost. I just hope that this replacement unit works properly. Because I don't see how anyone can fly it the way it responds. It just can't be that hard to fly a drone, especially if it's a beginner level drone. The first drone I ever flew (TDR Sky Beetle, same as their HS190 drone was easy to get the hang of. This one should be just as easy, not a struggle just to try to hover and move it around a little bit. Hopefully it's just this unit, maybe it's a bad motherboard, the gyros, or something. But Holy Stone has been very good in trying to remedy this situation.

Edit: I just got the replacement from Holy Stone at no charge. This one works. It is controllable. I do have to get the feel of flying it as this is only the 2nd drone I have ever flown. One thing about the props, they're brittle and break easily in spite of having prop guards. I broke the two front props on the faulty unit and I just broke a prop on the new one. I have to fly it in more open areas where there's nothing to hit until I become more proficient at it. So I now have a set of spare motors that was sent to me plus I can keep the faulty unit for spare parts except the mother board, that's what's faulty. So Holy Stone has great customer service! I went from 1 star to 4, can't give a 5 because of the 1st unit.

Final Edit: I've had the replacement unit for a while now. So I did a little experiment with the original faulty drone. I used the radio Tx from the replacement drone on the faulty drone and it works perfectly. So the problem was not the drone itself but the radio Tx that it came with. Thank you Holy Stone for helping me to get a working drone! Upgraded to 5 stars. Also I should add that I have been flying it a lot and improving my skills. This is a very responsive drone and can fly pretty fast at the expert level although I am mostly sticking to the mid level right now.

text:

The major problem I have had with this is the paint job is terrible. The dark silver has chipped all over the place. The paint's adhesion was so bad that every place that I put shoe goo to reinforce the body the paint just peeled off in that section and the shoe goo was not able to strengthen the body. I had to try to color match the paint and touch up the body after 2 races. The body is too thick and is prone to cracking especially around the pre cut rear vents. I got this pre-painted body because I lost the decals and window masks to another body I was going to paint and didn't have time to paint one before a race last minute.

There are two other people at the track that have the same body. They have not had the same issue with the paint cracking and flaking they probably did a crappy job on mine. The decal above the windshield was on so crooked that I tried to remove it and straighten it out but it got damaged in the process and I just had to take it off.

I have a closet full of board games. Our family is into playing board games together. My kids' interest is shifting toward card games lately and when I came across Dominion I thought it might be right up their alley. The cards that are included offer a variety of game play options right out of the box. Each game can be extremely different from the one before it, simply based on the cards that you choose to play with. For me, this is one of the best aspects of the game. So if you're looking for a game that the whole family can enjoy, you're sure to like this one!

title: Maybe it's just how we play?
text:
Let me start this off by stating that I've played this game 2 times: the first time with 6 people and the second time with 4 people. All told, it's been about 9 hours of gameplay.

I'm confident that this game has earned at least 3 stars.
Pros:
- The game is very well detailed, with excellent descriptions for every minute element.

-Monsters and challenges are numerous enough that you aren't fighting or trying to solve the same thing over and over again.

- Multiple Elder bosses to choose from and fight means lots of potential game sessions.

- Enough moving parts to create that "crisis" feeling that gets your adrenaline going.

- Actions and Challenges that can be failed. It's very easy to spend 30-40 minutes just trying to beat one difficult problem.

Cons:

- PLEASE MAKE IT GO FASTER. We don't know what the problem is, but after 4 hours and only getting the first of three challenges done, it gets really dull. We've tried placing time limits on individual turns, but it still takes about 5 minutes for each person's turn (including their encounter phase). With just 4 people, that's turns of about 20 minutes (if everything goes according to plan). If you fail two turns in a row to complete an action, you've now done nothing for 40 minutes. With only 12 turns, that's 240 minutes (4 hours).

My initial reaction was to assume that we were doing it slower than usual, since we were new. But after playing for quite a bit, we've become pretty objective-oriented. Additionally, it would be hard to go faster, since you do have to read things to get in the proper mood.

In any case, we found this game hard to enjoy after spending so long on each turn. The creative challenges and unique monsters became mere objects in our desire to finally get through this endless game.

I would gladly research how to improve this game, but I'm no longer sure that it would be worth it.

title: Good looks, but has many issues
text:
[[VIDEOID:2a34a1225f282a43a01cb9dee702fd6e]] I purchased the Style-B wheels in black. Let's start with the good. These look good. After testing tires from multiple brands I can say mounting tires was very easy and fitment was good. Unfortunately that is where the good ends. There are multiple problems with the wheels I received. We will start with either my package was labeled wrong or the item listing is wrong. As I said I purchased the Type-B wheels. I recieved a package that said Type-B, but they are actually the wheels labeled Type-C in the listing. The next issue is the screws that are included are very bad quality. I broke most of them with very little force. I ended up using my own hardware to build them. You are going to want to have your own hardware for these. You'll need m1.4x8 or m1.4x5 depending on the configuration you want to use. That takes us into the next problem. These come with a +4mm hub adapter and some brass extended nuts. They do not work together. The nuts are about 2mm too long and will not tighten the wheel down on an SCX24/AX24 axle. The alternative it to run these without the hub extension, but even that is not possible without also having extended hexes. The wheel face it too thin and normal nuts will not tighten down to the wheel. I was able to get these to work by running them without the hub extension and using a +7mm hex extension behind them. Side note to this, considering the included nuts fit the SCX24 axle shafts, they will not fit on a TRX4M as the listing says they will. The last prblem is more of an annoyance than issue. Due to the number of spokes vs the number of screws, it is possible to assemble these in a way that the outer and inner portions of the wheel don't line up. Over all I would recomend finding a different wheel option unless you are ok with having to buy more parts to make them work. If you happen to have some +7mm hexes and good hardware already as I did, these aren't a terrible choice.

*Updats*
After using these for about an hour I can honestly say the good looks of these wheels do not even come close to making up for it's faults. The hex inserts on the wheels are not machined properly. In order to get the hex to fit in all the way (even a stock one) you have to apply a ton of force. I also was not able to get them to sit flat so all the wheels wobble while driving. I even tried known good aftermarket brass and aluminum hexes with no luck. These will now be going on my retired/broken comp rig that sits on a display shelf. That's about all they are good for.

title: a family favorite
text:
We purchased this for our son's second birthday present. We gave it to him the morning of his birthday party, so that we could have it set up for the kids to all play with that day. He loved it so much, that it is not only the only thing that he wanted to play with that day, but he refused to get off it to open the rest of his gifts... sharing was difficult that day. Luckily, some of our other ride on toys worked on it as well, so the kids were all able to have their own car to ride down in, and then they just waited in line. Much easier than having them all share the one rider (because, you know, toddlers). Our friends son left crying because he wanted to keep riding this as well. They bought this the next day for him.

One of the nice features on this is that there are stairs on either side, which make it easier for the kids to get up and down. I also really like that it is five pieces total (including the car), so being able to store it in the shed is easier when you can tetris the pieces.

We have now had the step 2 up & down roller coaster for one year. It is still a favorite, but not the only thing he plays with (thankfully). We keep this out in the yard set up all summer long, and I have been very impressed that the colors have not faded. A lot of our plastic childrens toys tend to fade in the sun over time. While I am sure that this might eventually fade, it has not in the one year that we have had it. This coming winter we are planning on setting it up in the basement, so our kids can enjoy in year round.

title: Ceaco's COMING TO LIFE Noah's Arc puzzle is a gorgeous, fantasical puzzle as well as just plain fun to do.
text:
Ceaco's COMING TO LIFE series of puzzles are addictive with the vibrant images, the creative theme, the well-cut pieces that can be picked up as a group easily without falling apart, and the clean edges of the pieces. While I wish for an insert of the puzzle image in a larger printout, my 67-year-old eyes with the help of a lighted magnifying glass (which I use often for puzzles) did just fine. This was a really fun puzzle, and I have all three current COMING TO LIFE puzzles and will search for new ones if they are produced. Ceaco does an excellent job of making quality puzzles with moderate thickness of pieces. Sometimes the thickness is over-rated; I've bought some of those "top" brands with thicker pieces and they are okay, even though I've experienced missing pieces with them which I never have with Ceaco and the thickness didn't guarantee how well they hold together.

This is a delightful puzzle to do. I can hardly wait to do the third in the series.

title: Gorgeous and high quality Art Scratch Set
text:
This set is beautiful! First of all, I will start with the stencils. They are way higher quality than I expected... they are plastic instead of cardboard like a lot of companies try to get away with, even higher-end companies like Faber Castel. The stencils will last a long time and can be used for other art projects too. There are 7 of them, and they feature cats, dogs, stars, suns, moons, happy faces, sad faces, paw prints, hearts, etc. The set also provides you with about 12 wooden styluses, which are used to scrape lines on the scratchboard. There are two different sizes. The scratchers are OK. They are made of wood, but are sanded so that they do not give you splinters at least. However, I have seen higher-end scratch art tools or styluses that have plastic handles/pen holders and a metal design tool/ scraper. Usually, the tool features several different styles of the metal design tool, all of which are interchangeable. It would be nice if this set came with one of those tools.

Regardless, that did not change how many stars I think this little set should get because despite the stylus being wooden, it still does its job and allows you to create beautiful scratch art! The set features 50 scratchboards, some of which have a gold base, some of which have a silver base, and the majority of which have a rainbow base. The scratchboards with the gold and silver base are subtle and elegant. I can think of several specific projects that these, in particular, would be perfect for. However, the scratchboards with the rainbow base are my favorite. They are so bright, beautiful and trippy looking! You never know what color will be revealed next as you scrape the black coating away. Each scratchboard is the perfect size (about the size of a greeting card) and is a thick cardstock - these would make great greeting cards once you get the hang of this new (to me anyway) art style. I think you could also create beautiful mandalas on one of these scratchboards.

I have included my first two attempts creating scratch art. I was just fooling around with the stencils to see what one can do, so the artwork is not great. However, you can at least get a good idea of the vibrancy of the gold and the bold pigmentation of the rainbow against the black background. I recommend this set to anyone - kids or adults, seasoned artists, or beginners who are just looking for something fun to do.

title: Great for teaching spatial math and boosting creativity for young kids!
text:
I received this product in exchange for my honest opinion - my opinions are still 100% my own!

The Dive Into Shapes geometry building set comes with 114 building pieces and 15 double-sided, shape-building cards to challenge, inspire and encourage children to work on geometry skills. The cards included vary in difficulty and seemingly build on concepts learned from the other cards. My six-year-old thought this was the greatest set and set to work right away building as many shapes from the cards as she could. She really loved the three dimensional shapes and I loved watching her think through the process of how to get to the shape. Each brightly colored card tells the child the number of pieces required to build the shape, along with a clear photo. It also follows up with a post-build challenge – to change the size or think more broadly about the shape and what else you can do.

Even my four-year-old was able to get in on the building action and enjoyed exploring her creative geometry side by building cubes, prisms and attempting a sphere. We had build-off challenges where the girls were each given the same pieces and challenged to make a particular shape.

title: Maybe it is actually an Indoor Swing...
text:
I wanted to select "I don't like it" because it is terrible outdoors. While the clips are handy the lines are not very long so unless a branch is only around 4 to 5 feet off the ground, the swing will be much too high. Also, I thought the adjustments on the sides would allow for making the swing level as branches usually are not but, the adjustment beads just don't seem to hold. I tried adjusting them so they were even and they still didn't hold. Finally, the seat is made out of some sort of laminated something and over time in the weather the layers separate.

Perhaps this would be a wonderful indoor swing if one were into putting swings inside. Something would still be needed to hang the swing clips from since the ropes are short. Maybe this swing might work for a time in a sheltered outdoor area such as a garage or porch, however based on the one we got I would predict that humidity and temperature fluctuation would still get to it eventually.

title: probably better for older kids
text:
my daughter is 7, and was a bit intrigued at getting the project mc2 crayon make up science kit to try out. however, i do have to say that, in my opinion, she is still a bit young for makeup. but for a one-time thing, we just forged ahead.

this kit included a crayon wheel with 6 colors, a lipstick mold (holds 3), 2 lipstick tubes, and a makeup compact. i think as far as accessories go to put your makeup in, that's sort of cool. now what you do need to get is coconut oil.

the colors included were purple, dark pink, light pink, blue, green, and orange. i personally found the green to be kind of weird for a blush/lipstick kit. but that's just me.

we found that the instructions weren't very specific about the amount of crayon melts we're supposed to use. so we sort of guessed at that. and i was a bit nervous about my daughter handling the hot cup, so i did that part for her. as far as a child doing this whole project independently, i'd say they should be a little older, just for safety's sake (and less mess).

it was sort of trial and error with the color mixing. personally, i think it's better to just use plain colors as opposed to weird swirls, but maybe that's the fun of it? it got kind of messy mixing this stuff up in our own cups. i'd rather maybe some disposable cups were provided? or maybe i should have thought ahead and just used paper cups.

now as far as the actual makeup, once it's cooled and set, it's usable. but the stuff was hard to wash off. i didn't think it worked well as a blush, as it seemed to be more shiny (or maybe i should say greasy).

they should maybe include an extra lipstick tube to hold the third lipstick. one concern i had was that the kit is made in china. i'm not sure if that is a red flag or not, but there is some concern about toys and paint sometimes that come from china.

overall, i think this was an okay product, but i'd think it might be better for someone a little older, for safety reasons. if i had to spend money on makeup, i'd probably just go with buying some actual makeup. but this was nice as a science experiment to see how the color melts reacted with the coconut oil, and how it solidified (liquids to solid states).

disclaimer: i received this product as a free sample to try out, and all opinions are my own.

title: Trash.
text:
Things to like about this figure.
-it’s a Michael Myers figure based on the original Halloween 2 (which is the sole reason it gets ANY stars)
-packaging & accessories
Sadly that’s about all that I was happy with.

Aesthetically this figure was one of the biggest let downs for me in a long time. While admittedly I am not the biggest Neca fan I can say that 95% of the time they can make a 7” figure look like what they intended it to look like with wonderful array of accessories (the fact the packaging is sometimes the one thing keeping the figure from falling apart is another matter)! This figure falls in that 5% of wtf? Compared to the promotional art and the prototype (which by the way was actually 12 inches tall) I can’t help but feel kinda falsely advertised to. Yes I understand the proto will always look great as it is made to sell the product but This things head sculpt looks like it was sculpted from a hot, toasted marshmallow.. and looks like he’s been eating plenty of them too (dude is a little plump!) If your company can make a 7” piece plastic look like Arnold Schwarzenegger, Sly Stallone, etc .. then there is NO reason this thing shouldn’t look like a modified Don Post Captain Kirk mask with the Warlock Stretch. Hopefully the retro clothed H2 Myers will wash the taste of this fail out of my mouth. I won’t hold my breath though.

title: Durable light weight protection for DJI Spark
text: The waterproof silicone protective body case cover by RCGEEK is a good quality made product for the  DJI Spark.  Was a little snug while putting it on but nothing more than you would expect.  Seems to be very durable while stretching and didn't tear while taking on or off.  The cover is easier to install and uninstall than skin stickers and provides more protection.  The silicone cover is very light weight and did not affect controlling my Spark in flight or my  flight times. If you fly in the summer or live in a high bug area and have landed your Spark and found it covered in bug guts, then the cover is for you.  It's a lot easier and safer to take the silicone cover off and clean it than to clean the Spark itself.  I also like the fact that it comes in 4 different colors; blue, black, clear and grey but I wish that it came in even more colors. Overall I am very satisfied with this product.  Great value for the price!

title: Good if you catch it at a 5-6 dollar sale.
text:
This is worth the 6 dollars I paid for it.
Cheap plastic, but functions well, didn't break after I opened, closed, and solved it to open again two times.
Solving for the first time took me under a minute.

Note to buyers: it arrives with the marble to the left from the latch, on the latch side. I had to spend 3 seconds to guide it into the latch, to open it. Placing the marble right over the latch let's you open the lid. You can then close it and slide the latch to the left again, releasing the marble into the left side, so it's easy to reopen. If you slide the latch (with the marble in it) to the right side, it falls into the labyrinth that requires you to guide the marble around the whole cube, so it reappears to the left of the latch. This is the solving process, that took me (an adult) one minute.

title: Well Built Robotic BB-8 Droid
text:
Despite unfavorable reviews about the Sphero Star Wars BB-8 Droid, I purchased one as a birthday gift for my wife. Not thinking too much about the quality or what it could do, we were both pleasantly surprised at BB-8. Once charged, and the APP downloaded to my wife's iPhone, we put the BB unit through it's paces. It does take some getting use to, but it is fun and cute. Our large tabby cat hates the droid, he looked at us with that "you must be kidding me" expression but didn't attempt to swat or tackle it.
To learn more about what others think about the droid, we watched a science video about the product. First, except for the two antenna, it is solidly built into an 1/8" thick-walled ball of high impact plastic. To look inside they cut it with a bandsaw as nothing else would work. Once out of the ball, the robot, yes it is a robot, was well built. The maker, Orbotix, manufactures other robotic products, another BB-8 droid is due out soon.
Is it for everyone? Probably not, but my wife likes it and that's what counts. Yes, I would purchase this again.

text:
This arrives squished flat in a fold-top acetate bag.
If giving as a gift, this would be difficult to wrap as it arrives. First, fluff it into shape, then either pop it into a standard gift bag or find an appropriately sized box to wrap. This would make a great gift for anyone of any age who loves stuffies, especially beasties, or who loved these guys in the Netflix movie "The Sea Beast".
They are cute, soft, cuddly, & adorable. Since they are sent flattened, when you take it out of the bag, you have to squish it into shape a bit. This is easy to do & only takes a couple minutes, 5 tops.
As an adult, this stuffie fits in the crook of my arm nicely & is comfortable to fall asleep with. For my 3yo nephew, it is almost the size of his chest & he loves to fall asleep cradling it to his chest with both arms wrapped around it. I would say that we fight over it when he comes to visit, but of course I always let him be the one to fall asleep with it. He's 3 & he loves to argue & haggle. We have fun with it.
This is my favorite beast from the movie, & I love that the manufacturer/seller made the baby version, which, of course, is cuter & thus cuddlier!
I highly recommend. Oh, excuse me, WE highly recommend! lol

title: Excellent intro-level microscope
text:
This comes exactly as advertised and I couldn't be happier with it. My 8 year old loves science but is still at an age where a bit of clumsiness is be expected. This device is simple and sturdy enough to meet the challenges of his age range, yet still provides a "Wow, cool!" level of magnification that will keep a kid interested. You get enough magnification to clearly see plant cell walls and motes of pollen.

It comes with glass plates and clips, as well as a bunch of pre-loaded plate samples like onion skin and earthworm bisection... but just as importantly, you can easily stick a quarter or a leaf under the lens with no fuss. That's crucial for kids who aren't yet ready for delicate, time-consuming procedures. For older kids, the plates come with clear instructions and are easy to assemble.

I can't lie... I've played with this as much as the kids have. It's just that much fun to look at everyday things under the lens. Strongly recommend for a school-aged kid's microscope, or even for an adult who just needs a quick and easy magnifier for small details on things like coins or jewels.

title: Durable and fun outfit for a bargain price
text:
While many people will boast of Melissa and Doug's high quality toys, I often find their products very hit or miss. In my experience a lot of their toys are great conceptually, but fall short with sloppy, chipped paint jobs and/or lack of durability.

That said, this costume is a clear winner for Melissa and Doug. The fabric quality and stitching for this fire chief outfit is top notch, and the added bullhorn and extinguisher are just the icing on top. This outfit isn't like anything you'd find at Party City (where costumes fall apart after wearing them just once). It's beautiful, bright, fun and a total bargain for $25. Pottery Barn Kids sells a similar outfit for three times this amount.

My 3.5 year old will probably get a year or year and a half of fun out of this before he outgrows it, but I know I'll save it for his baby brother to enjoy someday too. The fire extinguisher and bullhorn aren't as sturdy as the jacket and hat, but they're in good shape so far after countless falls on hard floor.

title: Must have for RC trucks
text: So I use these Raiden Racing dirt covers on all of my rc's and they work but they come at a price. They work great at keeping out rocks and large dirt but sand and fine dirt can still get through. My biggest issue is when you button it all up the rc heats up much quicker and can easily overheat if your not mindful. If you run large dual 40mm fans like on my Kraton 6S the fans will actually suck the covering in and block up the airflow. So if you run these I'd suggest getting a temp gun and checking your motor temp after every battery. I burned up the motor on my Slash and Typhon when Ive never had any motor issues until I started using dirt covers. They work well but there's a definite tradeoff on the cooling/airflow.

title: Fun despite problems
text:
So, I got this at Costco for about 1/2 the price and that definitely affects how I am reviewing it. I would be more irritated if I had spent $24 on it.
The product works because the fish have raised circles (each a different size) on the back of them. As the fish are inserted there is a peg that gets moved in the slot so the toy can tell which fish it is. This means that the fish can only be facing one direction when inserted, which frustrated my two year old. The fish bowl then says: "That was a (slight pause) [whatever color] fish." By the time the bowl has finished saying this my child has generally already gotten another one in his hand and is trying to put it in. I worry that the correlations will not be happening correctly because of this.
If you switch over to where it is asking for a specific fish color the peg locks into place. The bowl then tells the child to "insert" the fish of the color it asks for. (Really insert? Is that appropriate vocabulary for a child working to learn their colors?) Any fish with a smaller sized circle can fit through but not ones with larger circles. The bowl has trouble telling which fish has gone through when they do fit and often tells the child the wrong color.
Other comments, the toy is pretty loud and I wish there was some volume control. In addition, getting the fish out of the hole in the bottom isn't always easy and (unless you leave the plug out) require adult help. The hole is a bit small and I am glad I have small fingers so I can get them up in the toy to angle fish so they will come out more easily.
All that said, my son really enjoys playing with this. And seems to be picking up some of his colors after just under two days of having it. I just find that I have to play with him to help make sure that he isn't getting confused or told the wrong colors. (I was hoping this could be a busy toy for when I needed to get stuff like cooking done.) If you are prepared for that, you will probably really enjoy this game. Otherwise, you might want to pass.

title: Hard-Core Trek Aficionados Engage!!!
text: Anyone who's familiar with 20Q electronic games knows the low-down on these devices; You supply the answer(s) and 20Q asks a series of mountingly progressive questions until it discovers what's on your mind. Enter the Star Trek version of 20Q: A lot of fun if you're vastly familiar with all things Trek, from TOS to Enterprise and all 10 Theatrical Features as well, but probably less so for the occasional Trek Fan with mildly passing interest in Trek-lore. On the other hand, one's breadth of knowledge about the known Trek Universe will certainly broaden in scope after spending some time with this little mock galaxy-class cruiser. Asthetically speaking, it's clunky at best but resembles enough of the iconic vehicle to be just passable, barely (if you're looking for a handsome model to display on your desk, consider one of the versions from Polar Lights or ERTL, or Playmates if you don't want to build). But, that's not the point, rather, it reasonably services the need for hard-core Trekkers to expand their would-be knowledge of a range of realms from Starfleet Academia to otherworldly facts (Romulan, Vulcan, Tholian, blah-blah ad nauseum... oh yeah and my favorite; The Metrons). This 20Q appears to possess a wealth of facts known throughout the neighboring Quadrants that comprise the foundational makeup of the Star Trek Universe (heck, Gene might even be impressed). LLAP.

title: Not as Tonka Tough as I expected
text:
Got this for my parrot, figuring if it's "TONKA TOUGH" it would be safe to keep him entertained. We had a smaller Walmart-brand (China) fire engine with tiny buttons that he liked to press to make the siren sounds. It's lasted for years, even though the buttons are ragged, they are still intact.

I hoped these were just as tough, if not tougher. He loved the siren sounds, but within 1 hour of non-attended play, he pulled all 3 buttons off. I was able to reassemble but they were now detached. There are also tiny rubber solenoids under each button. I can't imagine this is entirely safe for children, since each of the parts is a swallow hazard. He also quickly separated the ladder into pieces. Not surprising for a parrot and if that was the only issue, I'd still give it 5 stars. The wheels are sturdy and cannot be pulled apart, so that's good.

Again, even though this was destroyed by a parrot (small-sized African Gray, not a Cockatoo or larger bird), the fact that the buttons so easily pulled out and exposed dangerous parts makes me advise caution.

Too bad too, because he LOVED the siren sounds.
