title: Well made, easy to assemble, and kids love it, but has several choking hazards
text:
Very nice indoor toy for the kids. it arrived well protected with all the pieces safe inside the box ready to be put together.

I completed assembly by myself in about half an hour, although an extra set of hands could have sped things up a little bit. All the pieces were nice and smooth with no splintering or rough spots. Another bonus is that unlike a lot of furniture items I’ve put together, all the holes on this item lined up perfectly, making it a breeze to insert the all the bolts/screws and tighten them up.

The worst part of the entire assembly process was the need to install one of the ropes in order to finish the rope climbing side. It comes with one pretty much already in place (just have to tie a knot), but the other rope is loose in the packaging, and you’re required to thread it and tie 10 knots in order to create the rope grid. The instructions were very helpful, showing exactly how to tie the knots, so this part wasn’t as bad as it could be.

Taking off 1 star because the ropes had a rubber end on them to keep them from unraveling, but those ends fell right off without much effort. This obviously presents a choking hazard if you’ve got smaller children around, which I do.

After it was assembled, the kids have loved it. They immediately started climbing all over it and climbing into the tent underneath. They’ve played with it off and on consistently since it’s been put up, showing that it has a lasting effect on them unlike toys they play with one time and then throw down, never to be played with again.

I’m pleased with the item and I would recommend this to others with young kids, but recommend watching out for the ends of the ropes. 4/5 stars.

UPDATE: It’s only been about a week since my original review, and I’ve already got to adjust it due to quality control issues that could prove harmful for kids.

Aside from the choking hazard previously mentioned (wraps around the end of the ropes just slide right off without much effort), I’ve now found a second choking hazard: the buttons that hold the fabric tent doors to the frame.

I was walking by and just happened to notice something shiny in the floor of the tent. I picked it up and found out it was the cap from one of the buttons that attach the fabric tent doors to the wooden frame (pictures included). This could be a very serious safety hazard if you’re like me and have a smaller child/children around as well as a toddler. I’m updating this review to 1/5 stars.

title: Busy
text:
There's a lot going on here - and it's GREAT!

This follows the mold of pretty much most every other LEGO City set...fairly heavy on the minifigs with some detailed buildings in which they can....do whatever it is they do. The combination is such that play value (or, er, DISPLAY value for us adults) is pretty optimized. I mean, here there is a taxi, a news truck, a crane, a police motorcycle, and a bunch of characters (cop, crook, newsie, cabbie, etc etc) all adding flavor to a grand opening of a donut shop. The toy store owner here must be happy at the added traffic (well, except for the crook...he's harsh).

The buildings themselves aren't overly large, so in the grand scheme of things you're getting added flavor (heh) for an overall LEGO City setup. As such, the building techniques aren't overly complicated though they do a remarkable job with the (relatively) limited brick count. In other words, it's fun to make.

And interesting - I mean, the donut launches off the building!

Very good set, again I found it best in combination with other LEGO City sets and a good addition to my town of LEGOpolis, though as a standalone it works pretty well. Lots of fun!

title: If you child likes Bluey, this is a fun toy to have - but it does have a couple of issues.
text:
I buy a lot of VTech toys for my child (for reference, she's 2 years old) and she plays with them all to an extent. I had previously purchased another play phone and she loved it. Bluey is something we watch as a family and she requests to watch it daily, so I thought the "Ring Ring phone" would be something she would use for imaginary play.

She absolutely loves it from all the voices of the characters to the little digitized screen of Bluey, Bingo, Bandit and Chilli (among others). I was sad that Muffin wasn't on this phone, which seemed surprising.

This phone acts like most of the other toy phones when you push a button and then a character says something, or the phone will ring. There are also some interactive parts where they would need to literally blow into the phone (for the Bluey watchers, it's part of keepy uppey) There's plenty for any child to do and enjoy.

Now for the deltas -
1) The screen is pretty dim and it's only a grey LCD. I think with today's technology, it should have been brighter and in color. It's a small screen and shouldn't be hard to implement.

2) The sound is fairly low; I understand the use of batteries could be an issue, but why not a rechargeable battery one and have the sound a bit louder.

If those 2 issues were rectified (and the price point stay close to the same), this would easily be a 5 star toy.

As is, it's a fun toy for the young Bluey fan.

title: Most of the reviews here are right on, so read them all
text:
I'm going to mirror what a lot of other reviewers have said. This makes for a nice gift, or the box for a small gift, like jewelry, gift cards, SMALL/THIN items, NOT as an every-day-wear kind of box. It doesn't have very many steps, but they are decently difficult for people who don't do puzzles all the time (but maybe not for small hands or for the easily-frustrated).

There are TWO compartments, and the second one is best geared for gift cards as it's shallow.

Mine smelled of fresh lacquer (like paint thinner, not booze) and the parts were REALLY tight and kinda stuck together, like they had been put together while the coatings hadn't quite cured yet.

Before I gifted it I operated it a number of times, start to finish, to make sure it opened when it should, but the outer finish isn't durable enough for this to be used as an every-day jewelry box. This is best used as a gift box, and something to put valuables in that are not accessed frequently, as the parts are liable to loosen up, and the finish might rub off.

But it was fun watching my wife kinda struggle with it :P

title: Good Kit - OK Harness
text:
Pretty good kit. Everything I needed and able to set up quickly by myself (about an hour). Having someone help when putting up the cable would have made it a bit easier. Unfortunately the small cable to wrap around one tree was way too short (5 ft) for me so had to go to Lowe’s and make a new one.

If you put it at the height recommended for kids (I did) it will be a decapitation hazard. I got fiberglass stakes used to mark driveways when snowplowing and put underneath when not using.

Harness provided is OK, but not ideal (or comfortable) for small kids so I bought a full body harness (BD Momentum). My 3 year old and most of her friends prefer using the swing, but 1 year old and other really small use the harness. I also don’t like the blue webbing lanyard provided for attaching the harness. It works and is safe, but too long and the clips aren’t easy to work. I switched to an old nylon climbing runner with regular climbing carabiners.

If doing again I’d probably buy components individually, but buying a kit seemed safer /easier and this one worked. Kids love it.

title: A fine choice for budding astronomers
text:
This is not merely a telescope for kids. It's a kit that encourages the user to keep a journal of what he/she observes. The telescope is brightly designed and in no way resembles a professional telescope, but it does do a surprisingly good job of magnifying objects.

The two AAA batteries that are required (not included in the set) are for the built-in red LED light to enable users to read their journal and moon map in the dark. The telescope itself does not require batteries to operate. To provide steadiness, a tripod is included so that the telescope can be set up on a level surface and enable the user to observe objects in the sky without excessive shakiness.

There are three eyepieces included, which affect magnification. The 22-page Sky Gazer's Activity Journal guides novices through the nighttime sky and the wonders it holds. More a scientific learning or hobby item than a traditional toy, the telescope is best suited for a child who can care for the item, has patience learning how to operate it, and enjoys spotting areas of the moon. The telescope brings the moon amazingly close and in sharp detail, especially on a clear night.

For kids who live in a rural area, this object should be great, but those living in urban and in many suburban areas, it may be a bit tough to see objects in the sky with so much light emanating from cities. And if youngsters will be outside with the telescope, don't forget the bug spray!

title: A Brick of Bricks
text:
A literal and figurative tank. While it lacks the impressive interior detailing of some of the more intricate models here on Amazon, this thing builds incredibly dense.

On the one hand I was a little disappointed that it lacked a detailed engine or interior crew compartment. On the other, the incredibly dense hull design is super sturdy, making it a lot the kids can actually play with when finished (as opposed to the more 'model like kits that are intricate but a little flimsy).

It's not the easiest build ever, with a lot of very similar parts, so little ones may need some adult assistance on the build itself. That said, once completed its much more of a true 'you' than some of the specific 'model' kits you see here (I'm looking at you, Cobi).

Long story short, if you're looking to build an authentic main battle tank for display purposes, this probably isn't for you. If you're looking for something the kids can good around with after construction? It's about perfect.

title: Tiny Arcade with Big Surprises!
text:
When I first received an alert that these Tiny Arcade machines were on sale for under $20, I was a bit skeptical of the product at first. There have been hundreds of these kinds of players out there that you can find at your local stores in the clearance section, but for those that reviewed these said they were pretty cool for what they were. Interested, I decided to pick up a few different games to see how they hold up.

The packaging has a small cutout for a demo mode. This "demo" is actually an attract mode that shuts off after it runs through the sequence. To play the game, you have to unbox the unit and then power cycle it to start the game up. Speaking of powering up, one big surprise from the unit was the light-up marquee. It looks great while powered on and adds a bit to the arcade authenticity.

The arcade panel itself looks great. The stickers on the panel are evenly applied and the print quality is excellent. This defiantly looks great on display (I currently have three different Tiny Arcade units on my desk with one on the way).

For its size, the unit does a decent job replicating the Ms. Pac-Man experience. The buttons and the sticks appear to be using really tiny micro-switches unlike the mushy pads that other players tend to use. This made playing on the unit, despite its small size, actually viable. Unfortunately, those looking for an arcade ROM on-board will be disappointed. While it isn't an NES/Famicom version of the game like many other players, it is a modified version of the arcade version designed around the hardware.

Sound emulation is decent (appears to be full speed), but there are a few differences seasoned Ms. Pac-Man players will notice. One of the biggest differences is what happens when you eat a power pellet. On arcade hardware, the power-up sound plays through the entire time. On this unit, it plays for a few seconds then cuts out. Not a deal-breaker since everything else sounds fine to me. However, one thing to note is that it is impossible to mute the Tiny Arcade. Sound is always on, and it can be quite loud at times.

The unit requires 3x AAA batteries to operate. Fortunately, they come pre-installed in the unit. One thing I would have liked was the option for power over USB, but sadly this is not an option. Furthermore, the unit does not stay powered on during the attract mode, so those looking for a device to stay powered on full-time for display purposes won't find that here.

Overall, this is an excellent little unit for those looking for something fun to put on their desk. It's surprisingly playable given its size and there was some care put into the unit to not make it seem like a bargain-bin experience. The controls feel responsive and the screen looks decent given its small size, but a lack of USB power for an always-on attract mode and no sound toggle take a star off my rating. Overall, these are a fantastic purchase for anyone wanting something small and retro to display on their desk at home, at work, or in a video game / arcade collection.

text:
Pros
* This is a very cute product from LeapFrog - I'm not surprised - this brand always seems to hit the mark.
* Appealing music/sounds and toy itself is appealing to child to play with.
* Button on top of stovetop that sizzles when you put the pan on top - very cute!
* The play food is perfect and appealing for little hands. The pieces of food (slices of pizza and slices of bread) connect together and come apart, which makes the play more versatile and fun. Comes with a spatula for scooping or cutting the food.
* All parts store nicely inside the oven. Nice for clean up!

Cons
* While I know it is a counting toy, child is asked to identify the written numbers. This is more a task for an older child. My two year old won't be able to correctly pick the correct visual number when it asks you to move the dial to make the match.

These adventures reward you with extra resources or vp's for success without too much damage if you fail! Neat! This module also allows to CUSTOMIZE your mechs and make them totally unique from the other players! Sweet!
-THE GUARDIANS OF THE COUNCIL: This module adds a whole new set of 6 mechs (and miniatures) that are faction neutral. This workers/mechs that act like an extra worker but without the need for resources to activate them. They behave like drones and do not need a worker placed inside them to control them! Each one of these mechs also has a special worker's space unique to itself!! Awesome!

If you got the bucks, GET THIS! NOW!

title: Mold accumulates inside
text: I used this product once at my daughter's birthday party and the normal hose water is way too cold for little kids to play in, even on a hot day. They didn't like it at all. This would only be good for a person who has hot/cold water faucet outside to hook the hose up to so that the water temperature could be adjusted. I let the splash pad dry out for over 24 hours and then stored it for about 5 days when we used it again on a day that was over 100 degrees. Same thing, the water was cold and the kids didn't like it, even in that much heat. The real problem was that black mold had built up inside and it was shooting out of the holes as the water pushed it through. Black chunks were floating in the water in the splash pad and getting on the kids' skin, too. There isn't a good way to dry the pad out, since the water is always accumulating in some place around the outer ring. I really wanted to return this item, but once I had returned home from the trip we were on where we took the pad with us, over 1 month had already passed. It has really been a waste of money for me.

title: An unexpected surprise!
text:
My son is ten months old and "cruising" but not yet walking. We bought this toy because it had good reviews and looked fun for him.
We started with the legs on, but after he "climbed" up the toy and fell over a few times the legs were removed. So, as the other reviews said - if your kiddo isn't walking yet leave the legs off.
The second week we had the toy, my son did slam the laptop lid down on his fingers. He isn't old enough to understand cause and effect to that detail, so he didn't understand that by pushing down on the lid with his other hand he was causing himself more pain. He screamed and cried, but got over it quickly. It hasn't happened again (2 weeks later) so think he learned his lesson... This is a silly reason not to buy the toy. It didn't amputate his finger. It just hurt a little.
I didn't like that the phone wasn't attached, but for about a week it was all my son teethed on - so it ended up working out nicely. Now it is lost in the "black hole" of toys... but who cares!? He doesn't and it's his toy.
When we removed the legs, we stacked them and set them by the door to be put up later. However, my son found them first (there's nothing unsafe about them). My son loves the legs almost more than the toy. He bangs on them like a drum. He uses one to hit another and thinks the loud bang is great. We play "swords" with them.
The mode switch is right on the top so my son constantly plays with it. I wish they had placed the switch in a less conspicuous spot... I find this to be a design flaw. Eventually, the baby will wear the switch out. They're not rated to that kind of abuse. I don't mind the Spanish mode. I found it a little offensive others complained about it, and I am as white as you can be. :-) I mean, it's 2011. Diversity is in. Get over it.
Overall, it's a cute toy. Reasonably priced. The few gripes I have are smaller than the overall satisfaction with the toy, so I recommend it.

title: Great floaty idea, but quickly developed a leak
text:
This was great the first day my daughter and her friend used it. But after the second day the seam had developed a leak. Total bummer, because there were a lot of positives to this. Also, before I go into those, it is worth noting you may want a pump/inflator with this floaty. It's that big. I blew it up by mouth, but it took a fair amount of time. Note: There are multiple zones to be inflate.

POSITIVES
+The structure of this was appealing because the kids could pull themselves up through the center or over the side
+Likewise, if someone gets stuck underneath, they don't panic like they might with a large raft without a center opening
+Good size for a few adolescents but probably a little small for 3 adults

NEGATIVES
-If you blow this up by mouth, there were times where I would top off the air levels. However, when it is nearly fully inflated, it can be hard to get your head into the space comfortably to inflate it further.
-Because it blew out in the seam and it was where a right angle was positioned, it would be hard to patch

title: Great fun for my son & me
text:
Rating A & A Europe 1940 5 stars for fun game play, ruleset, quality of pieces & board.

I recommend this game to anyone who has played Axis and Allies 1942 and loved it, but wanted even more detail. If you haven't played A&A 1942 then Europe 1940 probably isn't the best starting point for getting into Axis and Allies.

My son and I play many variations of Axis and Allies are very experienced Axis & Allies players. For us, Europe 1940 was the ultimate - the game we'd been waiting for. It's hard to live up to such expectations, but Europe 1940 does. We've played Europe 1940 four times now (in 5 weeks if that helps give an idea of how much we like this game). We like the detailed maps (better than A&A 1942). One particularly interesting "feature" is the marsh that basically separates North from South Russia and can make Germany decide if it will split its forces as it pushes into Russia. I believe the luftwaffe is even more critical in this version than in A&A 1942.

Italy - good luck! So much to do, so little money. France - the pieces look good sitting in the box. They're on the board so briefly. By the time Germany and Italy are finished in round 1 France is lucky to have a couple destroyers, a plane, and a few infantry. Yet, the game is so balanced that France can still be a deciding factor. Viva la France!

We haven't put the Europe 1940 & Pacific 1940 boards together yet (spatial constraints until summertime), but we're pretty eager to combine the boards.

The rules are well thought and well written. Rules include national objectives, and also the rationale behind the objective (e.g: control of vital Soviet oil production; propaganda value and spread of communism), so not just the quantity of points but also some political/military/historical reasoning went into this. There seems to be less ambiguity in Europe 1940 ruleset than in some of the other Axis & Allies board games.

text:
The actual doll itself, naked, is absolutely perfect. I've redressed it and added some human earrings and she looks absolutely fabulous – unquestionably five stars!

However, the doll did not come out of the box that way and there are a few things that need to be addressed.

Let's start with the easy stuff:

Her clothes are now currently redistributed among my other monster high dolls. CA Cupid (diary edition) is wearing the dress, zombie shakes meowlody has the top with the fuzzy black shoulder cuffs, and until two days ago, haunt the Casbah Abby had the boots. (This is the only legitimate way I know how to get the Jane boots new as the Chinese knockoffs often seen on eBay are missing the feathers on the side of the one boot and have a hole where the feathers should be) The rest of it was put away in my various storage containers for the purpose organized by type of clothing. I literally don't have a single doll to put them on that they would look right on at the moment and I have several dozen dolls from this line and ever after high combined to choose from.

I bring the clothes issue up, because, on average, approximately half the price of the doll is usually the outfit – and most of this outfit is unusable. Yes I know there's another Jane doll out currently, but there wasn't one I bought this one, and I don't even like the new one anyway. Remember, this particular Jane doll itself in my opinion is perfect – it's just her outfit I have problems with……… And one major issue.

Jane was used to launch a very gimmicky note passing system involving the pets of the dolls. Her pet itself would've been cute if it didn't have a big hole in its back; but because it does, it just makes me think of vivisection and I can't help but think that the little guys in pain when I look at him – even if that does sound attracted dramatic.

The walking stick that turns into a pen looks really cool but has a tendency to open up in my purse, getting ink over everything and making it pretty much useless to me to travel with.

The tiny sheets of paper supplied with the doll that are supposed to be stuffed into the pet after being removed from the purse written on by the walking stick are just that – TINY! Impractical, smudgy, and kind of annoying.

On the bright side the red headband was salvageable.... And I still like her hairdo.

I just think this doll deserves more stars than I can ethically give it simply because there wasn't enough time spent on it during its development into a final product. The fact that the pen alone that doesn't seal, occasionally causing stains on the inside of the person's clothing makes me believe that this particular project wasn't thought all the way through

title: Take note: no volume or mute button at all..!!!
text:
Consider yourself warned!! You must know this is a miniature yet, bulky mechanical plastic toy.. Calling it a remote control is wrong. This does not have a remote to guide it but, rather just an on/off switch. There is no volume or mute- (warning applies here by the way!!) imagine a hollow sounding speaker placed inside a rattley plastic toy- with a few quirky sounding song tidbits.. (5 total I believe!) and equally noisy is the robotic mechanic noises of movement.. totally eye-catching and entertaining when turned on, after watching the toy “crab dance” through the loop of the songs.. You realize, this repeats itself- doing the same movements: Crabwalk forward- wiggle/prance on all 8 legs.. crabwalk back- wiggle/prance on all 8 legs.. Pause! New song and repeat!!!

Once you’ve seen the duration of the loop you’ve seen it all… Kids can probably handle x2-3 loops longer then adults- but, even a silly gimmick toy made for sheer mindless entertainment has its limitations! Arriving from the Easter bunny in a basket- not even 5min. into the looping I found myself looking for a volume/mute button… as, this would have made all the difference mind you- We even went looking for a sound wire we could clip.. bc, that was the extent of tolerating this due to the obnoxious factor.. there is not volume/mute!!

Now, if you can believe this… I think the best way for these to be enjoyed is getting two of them!! At least they dance together and feed off one another.. i’m not certain if music overlaps one another but.. otherwise they become rather repetitive on their own rather quickly. (kids may not care!)

For any who’s seen original Toy story series- remember Syd the neighbor used a doll head on spider legs?! It was scary but, sadly quirky cute in movie?!! Well, this reminds me of that- I’ll give it “uniqueness” for sure! Keep in mind.. 8mo. old recipient was terrified when turned on- So, that is something to consider. I see these being used as an office prank or entertainment, or younger ages 3+ bc, it might just be enough to hold their attention for a quick minute. The crab legs can be a little ominous but, this is balanced with a computer animated smile to look happy and less threatening! The Wally computer headed structure on top is where the on/off is found. These take x3 AA- and you must have a TINY screwdriver to release the compartment lid!!

This is one of those toys that I say… To each his own! It will either be fun or make you crazy and I fell in the latter category. At a price point of $10 it’s not a big investment if, not used every day. I hope this info can help your decision… Feel free to let me know!

I did noticed that this Lipo pack, does seem to put out more power than my other HRB Lipos. It is rated at 100C, so that might have to do with the extra power of the cell. When testing it, I did also noticed that the cell was warm to the touch, but not hot enough to burn you. I was popping wheelies and doing standing back flips with my Notorious, like it was effortless.

Overall, I must say, I am impressed with this new Yowoo Lipo. I believe is money well spent. I will try it on my other cars, such as the Arrma Talion, and Kraton. I'll see how it performs. But so far, so good.

I would definitely recommend it to anyone else.

One of them referenes a tiny 1 inch cardboard box - but of course that was not included.  How freakin cheap can you be???  Looking back I realize I did not read the contents carefully enough before purchasing.  It just didn't occur to me that I needed to be a magician in order to verify what parts would be needed in a beginners magic set.  I assumed for the good $ I was paying it would include basic items or at least referene where/how to get/build them.  The only magic the creator of this set has achieved is a sweet product markup for their wallet.  I do not understand how anyone could be giving high ratings for this product.  Save yourself from that feeling of disappointing your kid and look for something else.
I love working puzzles

title: Easy to use, and works. A full shuffle in a minute or less.
text:
So far after a month or so this card shuffler works very well for me with playing cards of regular size. Most times I can just cut the cards, turn the handle, and after four times through the shuffler the cards are well shuffled. Sometimes cards can jam if the handle is turned too quickly or slowly, and of course the top cards won't change order if the two halves of the deck aren't the same size, but those issues are easily fixed. This shuffler also works for some cards other than playing cards if the size is right--for example, I have the game "Set" and that game's cards can be shuffled with this shuffler.

I once bought an electric shuffler and it didn't work, and I never tried another one. If I had known about this manual shuffler and how well it works, I would have bought one a long time ago.

I purchased this for my 2. 3/4 yr old granddaughter and her 3 yr old friends. The splash pad was a huge hit! The kids played in it for 2 hours, had lunch, napped and played in it for another hour. Although it was our first day, the splash pad seems durable and VERY easy to assemble and use.

We had 3 3 yr olds on the pad. I don’t think there is room for too many more kids, but I’m sure we’ll try.

My only concern is that we live in a drought area, and I don’t think I’ll use it as much as the kids would like to use it due to water restrictions. It was probably the best $10 I have spent in a while.

title: zooming back into childhood..
text:
being an incurable fan of the series and a real-life F-body freak i want to add my 2 cents to the rest of the happy reviews:
i couldnt resist having back a radio controlled KITT after my battery-operated KITT was left next to the chimney on a cold winter night and i woke up the next day to see a flake of melted plastic instead, 25 years ago.
i'm 32 and i still got a huge amount of fun 'driving' this beautiful toy around the house. the engine does go
fast and the steering crisp and immediate. the scanner light is awesome, i just wish the headlights would go up but at least the foglights are there and working. there are no rear lights (could have been a great added detail and like every molded plastic toy, doors, hood, and t-tops are non movable). i dont use the voice effects (too noisy) but they're a nice touch. the detailing of KITT's aggressive nose is what made me buy it and ship it all the way to lebanon. the car looks amazing, drives fast and for me, holds sentimental value beyond the 109$ total (toy price: 36$, overseas shipping: 48$, customs tax: 25$) that i had to fork out for it.
Boys will stay boys (:

title: What a Creep
text:
Jack Ryder is the Creeper. His origins of old are that a combination of a crazy Halloween costume and some chemicals and devices change him to the Creeper (which he can do at will). Newer origins include that the Creeper is a demon of sorts. He has fast healing, super strength, stamina, agility, a painful laugh and a crazy personality in Creeper form. Not exactly Gotham's premier super hero (there's another you may have heard of) but he's there.

While the sculpting is good the character design leaves a lot to be desired (not Mattel's fault but there it is). He's a naked dude with gloves, boots, under wear and a really hairy back. The crazy face, maniacal grin and clawed hands look fine as do the detail on the teeth and fur. He's on the thin muscular body. The hair is finely detailed as well.

However, color wise he's sickly yellow with green hair and briefs, red boots and gloves with black trim and red back fur. It's an eclectic design to be sure but wow is it ugly.

He actually has one of the better neck joints on this line I've seen in a while with ball joint that also allows some forward and back movement. His arms have ball and pin shoulders / biceps, double pin elbows and pin/ball wrists. His waist is a cut joint and he has an ab crunch. From the waist down he has universal hip joints, cut thighs, double pin knees and pin ankles. He's no slouch in the articulation department.

He has his piece of collect and connect figure Bane and nothing else.

Technically I can't fault him in sculpt or articulation. But my goodness that color scheme and overall look is ugly. That may be the point with this character and if you are a fan I'm sure your score will be higher but for me he's 3 ½ and rounding down to 3.

Bane is the tactical genius and venom user who broke Batman's back. As simplistic as his design is they somehow managed to make this a great figure. The sculpt is amazing with little details like the eyelets, stitching and bottoms on his boots, and like the zipper on his mask all hiding in there. His massive chest and arms look great as does the skin tone used. And speaking of the paint it's simple yet effective as well. The boots are a cool high gloss, the gloves more detailed than I thought they'd be and the mask looks perfect. Even his venom dispenser and tubing looks great. He's also as articulated as the smaller figures although some of the joints may differ. Bane is not as hulking as some recent C and C's but still huge - about 8 inches - in comparison to the regular figures. He's a surprising 5 star figure for me.

title: Head Over Heels For this Cave Club!
text:
I have an almost five year old who went crazy over this cute T-Rex, and the adorable cave girl this set comes with! She kept telling me she wanted a cave club, and when this came out of the package all you could hear was a little girls screams of happiness!

To start (and I'm sorry for no pictures, but I couldn't get my phone in edgewise with her running off with it), this is actually a big set with a huge dinosaur that the cave girl can actually ride. It has a built on saddle with little holders that you can stick her legs in, and it has four, which means two of the people can ride the dinosaur. It also comes with a chicken leg, grapes, brush, a hair clip, and I think a cup. Again, daughter took off with it as fast as I got it out of the packaging. The dinosaur also has a little switch on the back of it's head where, when pushed, will open or close it's mouth. I was afraid that would be a little scary for her, but she loves it!

The Cave girl is super cute with chunky legs reminiscent of a Neanderthal, cute clothes, and I love the neon kinda 80's Flintstone vibe I get from the clothing and color choice. So far this is one of my daughter's favorite toys, and I can hear her playing with them in her room for hours on end! I'm going to get her a few more dolls to go with it, but she loves it!

title: Great deal for a handsome looking puzzle box
text:
For ~$10, this is a really good deal. It's roomy enough for some cash or a gift card, if that's what you're looking for, but also has plenty of room for a note or a small relatively flat trinket.

The "spine" of the book does have a little play to it, which makes it pretty obvious that this is a puzzle when someone picks it up. I modified mine with a pair of small magnets to remove the play so it could possibly pass as a book for a little while before the recipient catches on. Surprisingly, it's made of actual wood, so this was really easy to do.

The puzzle solution is 'simple', requiring only one trick, but could stump someone who isn't used to puzzles like this for a bit. Still, I don't think it would stump anyone forever. Also, despite being cheap, it's not too finnicky: if they try the right solution, it should work pretty reliably. It also looks way better in real life than I expected from a $10 puzzle.

Overall, this thing is really pretty impressive. I didn't really expect much from such a cheap puzzle box, but this is one I'd definitely recommend!

title: Edit* Please Read. Amazon changed this review to the wrong product.
text:
*Edit: this review is for the Retrogames Plus Anniversary Edition ONLY!

I have to say that I’m surprised how good quality this is.

Let’s start with the screen: bigger than some, smaller than others, best picture quality under $180 handheld category. It really does have such a good viewing angle that you can read text at nearly 90 degrees.

The dpad is in one, single piece and easy to use. That along with the front buttons makes any 8-bit, 16-bit, or 32-bit games. It even runs arcade and PlayStation games, though some tend to stutter more than others which make them unplayable without getting a headache. The joystick is comfortable enough to use but can be an issue for those that don’t like the recessed, concave-top types. The R&L shoulder buttons seem too loose for my taste. They are usable but I personally would like more stable shoulder buttons.

This system came with one 16GB internal SD for firmware and external 32GB for games. So upgrading the firmware from stock is so simple. Mine came with the latest open firmware so I really didn’t need it except it wasn’t in English or Spanish so I only changed firmware for that reason. It was the same version just a country change. You may not even want to bother since the games play the same either way. The firmware is excellent. It played any game I’ve thrown at is so far.

Back to the screen. My god the screen looks good. They even send with a screen protector to keep it looking good for years to come. I really like this system. The sound is ok. I can’t comment on it since I am not an audiophile. It sounds great to me, though.

I’ve tested quite a few of these gaming handhelds with my friend who raves about his PSP. Even he said this system had better controls and better quality screen than the latest PSP (for a fraction of the price I should add). Some games even run better on here than the PSP. Go figure.

title: THIS is the Droid you're looking for!
text:
Some really great design and engineering went into bringing this mini-robot to life. Great quality paint and detail. The silver looks very real and the blue parts are applied accurately vs. other R2 replica "toys". The iPhone App software is really well designed and has some fun features that leaves the possibility for expanding in the future.

The box packaging was exceptionally well designed and reflected high quality, like an Apple product. R2 is incredibly durable too. He's fallen off tables and beds and survives the occasional face plant. Still, he keeps going and going.

Among the best features setting the bar for R/C robotic toys, include the subtle movement they gave him when going from 2-3-2 leg transition and how he rocks back and forth with emotion, just like Kenny Baker did in the movies.

My only worry is that the company will inevitably stop supporting the App when iOS version XX.XX comes out in future years, making any current App obsolete. Who knows, really.. no company can commit to support forever. But not sure how much open-source-friendly technology there is in the body, but hopefully a user community of hackers will be able to keep the App support for this and other Sphero Star Wars robots alive, long into the future.

title: Great gift, Hard to assemble
text:
I bought this for my sons 9th birthday yesterday and he was extremely pleased with it.
It came as described, the mini llama and a few other pieces light up which is fun. It has a few weapons, a few misc items, 2 - 4 inch action figures, and a collectible. It also mostly contains lots of wall pieces. Now for some that could be a disappointment, for me its what I wanted and expected. We have the figurines and he wanted more building pieces and the giant tower.
The clock tower is a pain for an adult to assemble - do not expect your child to be able to manage it without your help. A couple extremely helpful hint - put it together on a very sturdy hard surface and start at the second floor - make that square then work your way up. Once the top is assembled THEN add the bottom 4 pieces, it took me 20 minutes of fighting with the bottom before discovering this was much easier and less frustrating. I also personally risked breaking the thing and used a very heavy bolt to smash some of the pieces into place because all my adult body weight pushing on it wasn't convincing them to go together and I got tired of hurting my thumbs. It's probably not recommended but it worked for me and my son now has a lovely assembled clock tower.

title: Cute & fun; good volume & on/off options
text:
[[VIDEOID:1f584e8c8624fc05f6413c576251bc59]] I've been around babies long enough to know that some toys seem like a great idea and are wonderful at first, but they can quickly wear on you with their sounds, or can be boring. For this reason, it's hard to choose a toy like this online without hearing it for yourself... I made a short video for this review to allow you to see and hear just a bit of the capabilities and sound.

I do like the ability to turn it on and off! Some toys with sound don't have this option, which is crazy and annoying and burns out the batteries. This also has the option for two different volume levels, which can help in the car or quiet living room vs. in a loud place where baby can't hear as well.

The little grey slider bar at the bottom of the "screen" doesn't do anything - it's just for show. So don't think you have control over brightness, fast forwarding, locking, or refreshing - despite the fact that those indicators are printed there.

Finally, the frustration-free instead of the standard packaging was great. I can't tell you how many times our kids received a gift, and then we had to snip an abundance of tough wires, ties, and/or tape to get it out of the package. The packaging for this makes it more fun right away for both the child and the parent when received as a gift!

title: The stylized animals actually make the puzzles a little harder
text:
You get two sturdy, wooden puzzles: a numbers puzzle and an alphabet puzzle. Each number or letter goes into an individual slot on the wooden back. Each number or letter has a deformed, stylized animal painted onto it. My 4.5-year-old niece actually found these more distracting than helpful as she kept trying to figure out the animal rather than seeing the number or letter. On the number puzzle, the six and the nine can almost fit in the other's slot, making the difference between the two less clear for her. I don't understand why they didn't make the nine with the straight line rather than a curving one, which would clear up this confusion. The puzzle has each number spelled under the correct spot, and under the animal number piece, there were lines showing how to write each number. Both my two-year-old niece and 4.5-year-old niece like tracing these lines.

For the alphabet puzzle, the name of each animal on the piece was below that slot on the puzzle. They chose some very odd animals, like newt for N. Again, my older niece was confused by the distorted animals with names she didn't know, though she did like unicorn for U. Of course, these puzzles were easy for my older niece but she likes playing with them, "helping" her younger sister to put them together. The two-year-old can put them together, but she prefers a numbers puzzle that is just number shapes (no animals forced into number shapes) and where the slots follow the contour of the numbers, making it easier to know which piece goes into which slot. Again, on the back under each letter, there were lines showing how to write the letter. I like that part, and my nieces do to.

title: Drives me crazy but the girls love it...
text:
My 5 year-old daughter and her preschool friends love everything Lalaloopsy, and we are already very happy owners of several of the full-size dolls as well as a number of mini Lalaloopsy figures. This is the first time we've tried one of the playsets, and while my personal reaction to the treehouse is pretty negative, my daughter and her friends really seem to love it.

This playset is very pretty, and has a lot of things for the little Lalaloopsy dolls to do, at least in theory. There's an elevator and a tire swing for the figures to ride, a little clubhouse to sit inside, several spots inside the trees to explore, a little paint bucket so you can pretend to paint the clubhouse, and on and on. As a parent, I find this playset to be extremely frustrating. The various pieces tip over easily, it's hard to make the little Lalaloopsies sit in their clubhouse or in the hammocks, and it's difficult to slide the elevator up and down. These things drive me crazy, but they haven't stopped my daughter and her best friend from playing with this set for hours and hours. The girls seem far more interested in pretending and imagining than in making things work exactly right, and the treehouse seems to be just perfect for that. While I truly hate to recommend it, I have to admit that it's made my daughter very happy, and that's undoubtedly what matters most.

title: Classic pet, well worth the money!
text:
"Your Sea Monkey pets may live up to two years"

That's a stone cold lie, but even with a short lifespan, these creatures are a MUST HAVE pet for every child! They're beyond easy to care for, fun to play with (you can pet them!) and they grow fast and big. The female ones are kind of ugly, but you'll want to take good care of them so they can make cute little babies that surprise you when you spot them! The "tank" is hard to clean, and you'll probably wind up buying all the little accessories that the company offers to help clean it, carry the monkeys around (I used to have the necklace), and give them "toys" to play with. I never managed to name mine, since they all look alike, but I still loved them and was sad when they passed. I believe this is a great pet to teach compassion for the smallest, faceless, buggy-eyed creatures. Perhaps the reason I don't eat animals is because I had sea monkeys back when I was a kid. Love these lil' shrimps, glad they're still selling them.

title: Works, but could be better
text:
We got this for our son's second birthday. The assembly wasn't bad. But like other reviewers have said, this trike is unstable. My son is still getting the hang of getting on it himself which usually ends up with him climbing on top of it to switch his feet around. It makes me nervous because it can topple easily. He also finds it fun to knock it over and pick it back up.

I love the safety bar feature which is why I picked this trike over others. My son is fascinated by wheels and I didn't want him trying to grab it while moving. It also works for popping our younger son in the seat for a spin.

My son is 35 inches tall and has a hard time reaching the pedals, especially if the wheel is turned. Considering that he's a tall 2 year old, I wish this bike had another closer seat setting.

I find the one hand maneuverability quite easy, but my mom struggled with it. You do also have to be careful because in a sharp turn, this trike will turn over with the child in it.

Overall I'm pretty happy with this trike and I hope we can use it for a while.

title: Great for experienced Gamers
text:
I like this game a lot. I think other reviewers have outlined it well. The instructions are not that well written, but I think that is partly because the game is hard to explain. Its easier to play it or see it played to understand how to do it. Friends of our introduced the game to us and I made them play it two nights in a row, then went out and bought the game to play with some family who were in town. Did I mention I liked this game a lot?

It is complicated enough to feel like you have actual control over what you are doing. There are plenty of option, and bits, and with the different decks (komplicated, improved) there is a lot of game to play before it will feel old, as it should be for the price. That said those family members who don't like to "read the cards" didn't like the game. My brother who plays lots of games like I do caught on almost immediately and won the first time he played (by one point). My mother got overwhelmed by the occupations and improvements. She felt like there was a lot of text and a lot of things going on, which there were. I probably should have stared her out on the "family version rules."

But I like this game. Take as a recommendation though that the family rules are really there for a reason, and not just for a "Agricola light" game.

I thought the concept of a cooperative game was genius and unique. It took a couple of turns to understand, but then it's lots of fun! It is suspenseful and keeps everyone engaged. Our kids are 9 and 7. I think this game is perfect for their age and maybe a little older as well.

Pros: engaging, tons of teamwork and strategy required, shared victory or loss, easy to learn-however I would always recommend reading the instructions and setting up without the kids, when you understand it, it's easier to explain to them quickly and then get started.

Cons: I can't think of any cons since I enjoyed this very much. I do think it's noteworthy that this is not a quick game like connect four or battleship, it takes a little while, but not an uncomfortable amount of time. Maybe 30-45 minutes.

title: Purple Phoenix Games Review
text:
One thing that has grown in popularity over the recent years are Escape Rooms. You know, where you’re physically trapped inside a room and have to solve various puzzles, crack codes, and beat the clock in an effort to get out before it’s game over. It should come as no surprise that this premise has made its way into the world of board gaming. Yeah, you’re not physically trapped somewhere, but you still have tons of puzzles to sort out in the fastest time you can. So how does this EXIT game hold up when compared with a real-life escape room? Keep reading to find out!

Disclaimer: In order to avoid spoilers, I will not be going too in depth with this review, but rather provide a general overview of the type of gameplay involved. Also, this review covers one specific EXIT game, but the general mechanics and gameplay are the same across the entire EXIT family.

In EXIT: The Game – The Polar Station (simply referred to as just EXIT from hereon out), you are a member of a research team stationed in the Arctic. One morning, the evacuation alarm goes off unexpectedly, and everyone makes a break for the helicopters. Just one problem for your crew – your exit door is already locked and sealed! You make your way to another section of the lab to look for an alternate escape route. What you find is a room full of locked drawers/doors. You must quickly crack these codes, in hopes that the materials contained within will aid you in your attempts to escape before the final rescue helicopter takes off.

To setup for a game, sort the cards into their appropriate decks – Riddle cards, Answer cards, and Help cards. Place the Decoder disk and the Book in the center of the table. Leave the other items in the game box, to be introduced later in the gameplay. You will also most likely need a pen/pencil and paper to help you as you solve the riddles. And bam! You’re ready to start. You may then open the Book and begin the game. The game ends if or when players are able to successfully solve all of the riddles/puzzles and make their escape from the polar station.

Without spoilers, that’s basically as much detail as I can provide. Over the course of the gameplay, players will be using the pages of the Book to find clues, solve puzzles, or even identify secret symbols. Riddle cards will be drawn and used as ciphers, puzzles, or clues to help crack a code. When you think you have the correct 3-digit code for a specific Riddle Card, enter the code onto the Decoder disk. The disk will then provide the number of an Answer card, which you will draw and check to see if you were correct or incorrect. If your answer is incorrect, you simply keep trying to solve the Riddle card. If your answer is correct, you will then be instructed to draw other Riddle Cards, or the other items from the game box, and will continue with these new puzzles. If at any point in time you feel stuck, you may draw a Help card for the corresponding puzzle. The first and second Help cards will give you hints, and the final Help card will tell you the solution to the puzzle. Draw these sparingly if you can, as they affect your end-game score!

When all puzzles/riddles/codes have been completed and cracked, the game is over. Players will then check the rulebook to see how many Stars were earned, out of 10. The number of Help cards you use, as well as how much time you took to complete the game, will affect the overall score.

All in all, I think that EXIT is a unique game. The games of the series have varying difficulty levels, and this particular EXIT is rated a 3 out of 5. So this one isn’t the most difficult game in the bunch, but it wasn’t easy either! All of the puzzles require creative solutions, and the answers are rarely ever as straight-forward as they appear. Some puzzles are more logical than others, while some require you to physically manipulate components to be used in creative ways. I guess that’s as good a segue as any to get into components. This game consists of a deck of cards, a Decoder disk, a Book, and a couple of special ‘items.’ All decent quality overall. But here’s the thing – you will have to bend/cut/manipulate/destroy many of the components to help you in your mission to solve the riddles. So this game is literally a one-and-done. It cannot be played again.

Did I enjoy my play of this EXIT game? Yes. It was uniquely challenging, while forcing me to think creatively when addressing the different riddles. The method used to solve one riddle is not necessarily the same to solve the next, so you have be able to adjust on the fly. And often times you will have several riddles in play at once, so you have to decide which to address and when, when do you have the right information, which riddle it goes with, etc.

The biggest drawback for me is that it cannot be played again, The fact that you have to alter the components to a point of destroying the original card is something that was personally hard for me to get used to. I try to keep all my games so nice and pristine, that having to cut a card apart was tough! I got over it though. Having played a couple of the EXIT games, as well as a few of the Unlock! games, I would have to say I prefer the Unlock! system. The puzzles are just as challenging and creative, but you do not need to alter components to complete the game. That way, I can pass along an Unlock! game to a friend, as opposed to just tossing this EXIT game right in the recycling bin. I might pick up another EXIT game if I had a specific group/game night in mind, but in general I don’t think I’ll be grabbing any more of these, for the lack of replayability alone. The gameplay itself is pretty great, but the fact that I can’t play it again is a con I can’t ignore. Purple Phoenix Games gives this one a chilling 4 / 6.

text: Everyone has seen these  common magnetic letters and numerals that stick to the fridge or other surfaces.  I ordered some for my 18 month old grandson thinking that it would be a good way to introduce him to letter recognition,  spelling, word sounds, etc.  It's a really simple product that doesn't require a lot of investigation. title: Well worth it!
text:
I purchased the S107 Metal series Blue model Heli and found it to be a great deal of fun. I originally planned to purchase one for each of my 3 nephews. I started out with the Execuheli. Well, it had a lot of pretty lights and a all plastic body. It did not by any means compare. Although both heli's are in the toy class, the 107 offers far more control and flight stability by comparison. There was however one draw back, Flight Time...This is a big thing for kids and well.., all those who wish to play. My flight times recorded anywhere from 6-7 mins. Concerned, I sought out an alternative. The S107G-19 replacement battery was the solution. When two fresh batteries are installed in parallel you will more than double your flight time. I went from 6-7 mins to 21-22 min flight. On the 23d min you are grounded. Recharging time is greatly increased to an 1 1/2 hours but again, "Well worth it"

P.S to reduce the charging time you might want to consider purchasing the wall charger.

title: Fits smaller puzzles too, but not all puzzles with pegs
text:
I bought this puzzle rack because I have puzzles of slightly varying sizes and brands that I wanted to store, and being a triangular type shape, this rack gave me the option to store smaller puzzles. The rack is sturdy. The two front posts/feet have protective caps so they won't scratch the floor. The back of the rack has no feet - the rounded back corner rests directly on the floor, so the rack is canted slightly, which keeps the puzzles more firmly in place. There is no protective covering on the back corner that rests on the floor but as long as your floors are level it doesn't appear to scratch.

Puzzles we own that FIT WELL include:

Schylling inlaid puzzles (we have the cow, train, and school bus) - 11-1/4 x 9-1/4 inches
Circo numbers and alphabet puzzles (pegless) - 11-3/4 x 9-1/4 inches
Goki lighthouse/sea scape - 11-3/4 x 8-1/4 inches

Chunky puzzles (like the Melissa and Doug Fire Engine) DO NOT FIT. The chunky pieces are too tall to fit between the rack shelves.

Pegged puzzles like Melissa and Doug See-Inside Shapes DO NOT fit because they have pegs near the edges of the puzzles and the pegs will not fit under the wire of the 'shelf' above. However, I have some 9-1/2 x 9-1/2 inch Montessori style botany and animal peg puzzles that DO fit as pegs in the top two-thirds of these puzzles are located in the middle section of the puzzle board, not near the edges (but please note, you need to leave an empty rack above them to accommodate the additional height of the pegs.) The ones I have that fit are the Turtle, Bird, Horse (slightly off center), Leaf, Tree, Flower. Others may fit, we just don't own them. Other peg puzzles (small pegs) may fit, as long as they do not have any pegs near the edges of the puzzle in the top two-thirds of the puzzle.

I also have some smaller, 6 x 6 inch puzzles that fit in the stand just fine, although they could slide out the side if the stand was tipped.

The other item I tried to store in the rack was Kid-O Magnatabs (A-Z and a-z) but they were too thick for the rack.

I wish the gap between the shelves were slightly larger, to accommodate peg puzzles and the Magnatabs (if so I'd be buying two of these racks instead of one), but overall, we have enough puzzles that do fit to make this a worthwhile purchase, and I do like the ability to store puzzles of different/non-standard dimensions.

title: Gbaby Wanted Real
text:
The Cullen's are the most popular vampires since Tom Cruise and Brad Pitt, Interview with Vampire (gave my age away there) - Stephanie Meyers Twilight saga has attained a cult like following and Mattel has delivered a set of dolls fans will love! Over the years I've been disappointed with male barbie dolls - even when the corresponding female doll was wonderful. Not so this time. Emmett is a very well crafted doll! The first thing I must say (in case you don't read any further) ... He has Real hair! No fake, plastic, 80's hair here! title: Family enjoys it!
text:
I bought this game and have played with people who played the computer game when they were young and kids that had heard of the old game but never played it. So far it has been a hit everytime. We had a group of 4 between ages 10-14 that kept playing it over and over. My brother and sister (in 30's) played a couple times and enjoyed it.

There are a couple rules that we weren't exactly sure of, but we just decided as a group what uncertain rules would be and it worked. Rules say play either a trail card or a supply card on your turn. We decided to just play supply cards as they were needed. A death card was drawn the first round and we decided that you couldn't die on a first round, but second round was fair game.

If you don't enjoy sitting back and watching the game play without you, it might not be the game for you. But even when one of us died, we still enjoyed the banter and watching to see if anyone else died. First game we played we ran out of supplies about 1/2 there and all died. Some games we have just barely made it there. I don't think that there has ever been a game that all the players made it safe. One game 2 players died on the last 2 cards played before we got to the finish. It reminded me of the computer game. There was a lot of death.

Would recommend to others. You could watch a video review online that could better show how to play. It's a fun team playing game trying to get everyone to Oregon.

title: Fun Game - But racist overtones
text:
We enjoyed this game, but some of the residential tiles have racist overtones. The absolute worst tile in the deck in the housing projects tile. It causes the user to lose 2 reputation points if placed near almost anything else. The predominant community stereotyped as living in Housing projects in the U.S. is the African American community - so I'm not sure what the intention is here. This tile can be contrasted with the Mobile Home Community tile - which is often just as poor of a community as those in the housing projects, but whose stereotype in the larger culture is more white. In the game, this tile does not penalize the user with reduced reputation. Again, why are the housing projects so much strategically worse than a similar economic community? Unfortunately, the absolute worst contrast is when looking at the tile playing off the creator's name, which would be cute if these other tiles weren't so bad - it's an overtly White German sounding residential area: "Burg Von Alspach." This tile is a much better residential tile than the other two, since the user gets increased reputation with this.
So, in short: The tile that most users would associate with the black American community is the worst in the game - which is juxtaposed with a strategically "neutral" mobile home community, and the overtly positive White European sounding tile.

There have to be other ways to get the variation required for residential tiles than by making tiles that connect to actual racial and economic communities, which also serve to reinforce ignorance about those communities. We'll be attempting to return it.

title: Pixel Perfect Paperweight Placed On Your Desk
text:
The PDP Pixel Pals Master Chief is a kind of a fun conversation piece that you can put on your desk.

The Pixel Pal Master Chief is about the size of your hand, and maybe an inch thick, so it has a solid enough base to sit on your desk without too much wobble. Even though Halo obviously isn't an 8 or 16-bit game, the pixel art here applies a retro design to the iconic 1st person shooter character. In the back there is a cover that you pop open and insert a couple AAA batteries into. At the top of the back is a straightfoward on/off sliding switch to turn on the LED light inside. When placed on your desk it in a well-lit room it looks ok, but the colors are a tad dull. However, it does appear rather striking when lit up in a dim or dark room.

So while it's a relatively inexpensive desktop collectable, I feel like it could have had a couple cheap modifications to improve it. At a minimum, I think there should be a tiny cut-away spot in the plastic so that you could hang it on a wall with small nail. From there, it would be a nice bonus if the switch was in an accessible place so that you could still turn it on while it's on a wall. Those modifications shouldn't have really altered the price. Finally, if it didn't add too much cost, it would be cool if the lights flashed, or if there was a light sensor that automatically turned it on when it gets dark.

Even with my wishlist features not included, it is kind of a dorky-cool collectable to put on your desk if you're a Halo fan. Essentially...what you see in the Amazon pictures is exactly what you think you're getting if you order this.

title: Great quality, beautiful puzzle!
text: This puzzle is absolutely beautiful! It looks just like the picture. The pieces are made of wood instead of cardboard and fit together nice and snug. You can actually pick up the completed puzzle without it falling apart. The letters on the back definitely help putting the puzzle together and the dividers in the box we're perfect for sorting. The pieces came in a pretty drawstring bag inside a sturdy box. It also comes with a full-size poster of the image. So if you need help you can assemble the puzzle on top of the poster as a guide. My only complaints would be that a lot of the pieces are the same shape and will fit in multiple spots. This becomes tricky when your filling in the background pieces because the color is only slightly different shades of blue/green. The trick we figured out was to turn the pieces over to see if the letters on the back line up. I also wish it came with instructions in English. For the puzzle it wasn't a big deal I could figure that out but inside the box was a packet of white powder. I had to do some digging to find out it's puzzle glue. You add water and paint the back of the puzzle to glue the finished piece together. The packet only have Chinese on it so I wasn't sure what to do with it. Over all it's a beautiful puzzle, great quality and worth the price. I would definitely buy another.

title: Sound effects not appropriate for young kids
text:
I bought this for my laser tag-obsessed 5 year old. I thought it would be fun for our family to play together or for him to play with his friends.

The good news is that he LOVES it. The accuracy issues others have mentioned aren’t a problem for us, it’s actually great for my little guy.

The bad news is that the only options for sound effects/weapons are “pistol”, “rifle”, “machine gun”, and “rocket.” And they are all pretty realistic sounding. Nothing more disturbing than seeing my sweet kid “blast” his friends with the rapid pop of a machine gun. Honestly it made me a little sick to my stomach and I DEFINITELY would not have purchased this for such a young one had I heard it first.

I wish there was a more PG/kid friendly option, like a “pew-pew” laser sound that wasn’t tied so directly to actual weapons of war and hunting.

This would get 5 stars for me if there were more options for sound effects, so for those of us that care about these things, heads up.

title: Our cats LOVE this little toy
text:
When they hear it switch on, they will all jump down from the bed upstairs and come running downstairs to play with it. The downside is they will chase it under the stove, behind a cabinet, under the couch, and generally places that are a pain to retrieve it from. That has limited how often we get it out for them to play with it, but when we do, they are obsessed. Lots of reviews say the battery life is horrible, so I got the extra batteries, but we are still on the original. Granted, we don't leave it out all day for them (it isn't a loud toy, but when it goes underneath something and starts vibrating against it, that can be very loud).

Full disclosure: on the second or third day of having this toy, one of our cats bit down on it, causing one of the legs to come off. The legs are tiny and not a choking or digestive concern, but this made it unbalanced, causing it to go in tiny circles and not move in straight lines anymore. I was able to find Hexbugs made for kids in the toy section of a local big box store, but without the fluffy tail. This makes the bug even more likely to go underneath things, so stick with the fluffy tailed version!

This Star Wars play set comes with the TIE Fighter (fighting machine) and one figurine (the TIE Fighter Pilot). The figurine is a good size (around 7 inches tall) and has articulated joints, so it can be posed. It appears to be solid and sturdy, and looks like it will survive the play of most children. All 4 of the available figurines have interchangeable parts, so the child can actually create his own "Hero" by mixing and matching the various parts from the other figurines (which are not included in this set--you have to buy the figurines separately or get them as a set along with their respective "fighting machines"). This added feature for creating their own hero fighter is great for the children, but not so great for the caretaker's pocketbooks, as, of course, that just about guarantees that the kids are going to want all 4 action figures! The TIE FIGHTER machine is also made of adequately sturdy plastic, and has two six-sided wings, which "convert" by folding in half. The "conversion" function is a little exaggerated, as, it doesn't really change the function or basic structure of the spacecraft. But, again, that is evaluating the toy from an adult's point of view.

The best reviewer of this product is my 8 year old grandson, and he really loves it. He loves anything Star Wars. This is the type of toy I also appreciate as a grandparent, as it is not a video game nor is it electronic, and it also definitely engages his imagination during play. Just a note, there is some basic assembly required for the spacecraft, and a younger child may require some adult assistance to put it together (however, the 8 year old had no problem snapping the pieces together). This is a good toy, and pretty standard as far as quality when it comes to today's plastic playthings. The MSRP is a little high, but it seems you are going to pay a premium for anything that has to do with Star Wars, anyway. I am sure most boys (and maybe even girls) ages 4 to 9 would love this set, and it is definitely a safe bet as a gift, especially if the child loves Star Wars.

title: Magical!
text:
What a fun addition to the real-world Harry Potter universe! This wand is a laser-scanned copy of the original movie prop, and it feels fantastic in the hand: solid and well balanced, easy to flick and wave and properly cast your Petronus. But be careful: there is a light at the tip of this wand, and you don't want to whack it into a wall or anything. But as a piece of Harry Potter memorabilia, this wand looks simply fantastic. (See the unboxing photos that accompany this review.)

And that lighted tip is the point of this "Wizarding World Harry Potter's Light Painting Wand." With the light on and the Wow! Stuff app downloaded, you can "paint" with light, and the app will record while you wave the wand and make patterns, spell words, etc. (Again, see photos.) To be clear, the end result is a still photo, not a video.

The Wow! Stuff app was easy to download (iOS), and installed in a matter of seconds. The features are few and straight forward (Record, Stop, Download, Go Back, etc.) There are also controls to let you limit the exposure time, or adjust the exposure (ISO), and even start a countdown timer so you can set your phone in place, then get in position before you start your recording. Note that the instructions (wisely) suggest you put your phone/iPad/etc. (whatever you are using to record) in a stable place where it won't be bumped or otherwise move. You're essentially doing a long-term exposure here, so the app can capture the tip of the lighted wand as it moves.

I will say that the version of the app I was testing was an early version, and still buggy. It would crash it's fair share, but it still worked and I'm sure future versions will not only be more stable, but also offer even more features.

Bottom line: so far, this Light Painting Wand has been a hit, allowing the little wizards and witches around the house to have a lot of fun casting "spells" and capturing them in their photo apps to show off and share.

title: Excellent Lego Set
text:
At first I thought this set was a little overpriced. It seemed more like a $40 set than a $60 set. However, I've come to feel the value is here. Each of the Banshees feels substantial. And, the terrain build with how it hooks up to both models to show an in-flight pose is very nice.

The minifigures are both nice as well, but I still feel the legs are a little odd, like a smidge too long. Neytiri's look feels a little off to me in Lego form, but Jake Soolee looks really good. I like that their hair pieces have an attachment point so that they can connect to the animals of Pandora. That was a smart inclusion by Lego.

The build took about two hours at a casual pace. It did feel a bit repetitious, but I purposefully built both of the banshees first and saved the terrain for last. (The instructions have you building the terrain in the middle of the two creatures.)

I was a little disappointed in how the wings attach to both creatures. The ratcheted connection type they went with is easy to knock off. It definitely seems more geared towards display than play. Ball joints may have looked ugly (since they always seem to be gray), but I feel would have been better for play and short term posing.

The terrain build is a vast improvement over what came with the AMP Suit set. It looks like a piece of Pandora and feels well thought out and fully developed.

I did find the Banshee jaw pieces a bit troublesome to put on. The fit is quite tight. I'd advise adults assisting children with them. Otherwise there wasn't anything too fancy, and kids should enjoy this set as well as adult Avatar or Lego fans.

The last thing I'll add is that it seems like Lego can just completely drop the pretense of not making military or violence themed toys. Superheroes and Star Wars was pushing it, but Avatar is a movie about the military wiping out an indigenous people with modern-style military weapons.

title: Great Value & Quality for Inquisitive Young Minds
text:
I bought this microscope for my nine year old son. He has been excitedly collecting all sorts of items from around the house and yard to inspect. The microscope is easy to learn and use and sufficiently durable, although I wouldn't classify it as a toy; and user error could certainly damage it. But, damage wouldn't be the fault of the manufacturer, as it is well made and simple.

Some of our (yes, even the adults in the family enjoy it) features:
* 4x, 10x, and 40x magnification
* Top and bottom lights for viewing solid and translucent substances
* Easy to use clips
* Comes with sufficient supplies to get started
* Easy to navigate instructions

After we unpacked and set up the microscope, we had a doctor-friend over who gave my son a bit of a tutorial. Not only was it helpful, but it gave a real-world impression of what the microscope can do. Her excitement as a respected professional was really significant in learning to appreciate the microscope.

title: Slapdash Paint Apps Shackle Syndulla and Stormtrooper
text:
After Disney bought Lucasfilm and decided to complete the “Star Wars” Skywalker film saga, I decided I finally had to cut back on the number of Hasbro action figures I was buying.

At the time, I was watching the CG animated series “Star Wars Rebels” on Disney XD and collecting the 3.75-inch action figures based on its characters, so I decided to complete that collection for as long as Hasbro made them.

“Stormtrooper Commander & Hera Syndulla” (MS19) is a two-pack in the “Star Wars Rebels” Mission Series (2014). The Stormtrooper Commander is a modified Stormtrooper (SL01) action figure from the 2014 “Star Wars Rebels” line with the addition of an orange pauldron, while Hera Syndulla is a brand-new debut figure.

Each figure has five points of articulation (5POA) and comes with one accessory: The Stormtrooper Commander has the standard BlasTech E-11 blaster rifle and Hera has her Blurrg-1120 holdout blaster.

I'll give this Mission Series set credit for not pairing Hera with another straight repack of the SL01 Stormtrooper, as main cast characters Zeb and Sabine were. The distinctive orange pauldron of the Stormtrooper Commander (which nicely complements Hera's orange flight suit) has always been eye-catching, even as far back as its debut in the original trilogy film “Star Wars: A New Hope.” But that's as impressive as this figure is. Hasbro's detailing on its 5POA Stormtroopers leaves something to be desired, such as its failure to paint the nine white molded dots above the figure's belt (they should be black).

In addition, the paint detailing on Hera is terribly lax. For example, although the mold meticulously reproduces the straps that hang from her belt and encircle both legs of her flight suit, the straps themselves are unpainted (they should be white). In addition, the brown strap holding her goggles and ear coverings in place is erroneously painted “on” her chin, while the animated character wears it “under” the chin.

There are other paint misapplications or omissions typical for a Hasbro 5POA offering: The eyepieces of Hera's goggles should be colored-in black. The straps connecting her goggles to her earpieces, and encircling them, should be silver. On the brown square just above her belt, there are three molded points (two dots and a rectangle) that should be painted orange. Finally, the “vamp” part of her boots should be painted white. (However, all these details are correct on the Hasbro 6-inch Black Series [TBS] version of Hera, No. 42.)

One bright note: The white patterning on Hera's leku is nicely done. Not sure if the pattern itself is screen-accurate, though.

Unfortunately, as of this writing, the MS19 Hera Syndulla is Hasbro's only 3.75-inch offering of the heroic character (whereas Sabine Wren received an impressive and single-carded update in 2016). This is a terrible oversight for a character who not only goes on to serve the Rebellion (listen for “General Syndulla” over the intercom in “Rogue One: A Star Wars Story”), but also survives the Galactic Civil War (see the final episode of “Star Wars Rebels”). Here's hoping Hera will eventually be as meticulously sculpted and painted for The Vintage Collection (TVC) as she was for TBS.

title: Awesome!!
text:
This thing is just plain awesome! :) This is the lightsaber of Kylo Ren, which became an immediate fan favorite once the first trailer for The Force Awakens debuted. What's so cool about this lightsaber is that it has smaller blades that make a cross guard. As soon as fans got one look at Kylo Ren's lightsaber, they wanted it. And now, you can have it!
This is a really neat lightsaber, and easily one of the coolest toy lightsabers I've seen. :) Now, this one isn't electronic, so there are no lights or sounds, but they do also make an electronic version if you want one with lights and sounds. Anyway, to extend the blades, all you need to do is flick your wrist. :) Now, some people who have purchased this one have mentioned having trouble getting the cross guard blades to come out, but I found that a strong, quick flick of the wrist usually does the trick. :) This lightsaber is very lightweight, so kids should have no trouble at all playing with it. :) It's also very easy to hold, either with just one hand or both hands. :)
All in all, this is a really cool toy, and I guarantee that kids will have a blast with it. :) Whether you're a kid or an adult, this thing is really cool and lots of fun. :) I would gladly recommend this lightsaber to anyone. :)
