title: Exactly What I Wanted
text:
Update: So after sorting 2000 cards (Totally sucked sorting them), yes, more than 6 multiples per color, more like 25-30 per, but most were 2 multiples, few 4, and no more than 4 per card at all. I was worried about these boxes and people getting 20 of the same cards from other sellers. SCG is Awesome!!!

If you're new to mtg, this will definitely help you out as long as you realize, this isn't a complete deck builder (at least not from what I got).
Of the 2 boxes (2000 cards "I think? I didn't count, but boxes were full") purchesd 2 days apart from each other I got a combined 100 basic lUpdateands, 52 foils, no more than 4 of a kind, with maybe 6 multiples per color. Nothing worth a lot which is good, cause without a ton of multiples, you're able to understand the cards, find a synergy and purchase the singles you need to complete your decks to perfection.
A bit of work is involved, which is what makes mtg so enjoyable.

You can play a deck with a $50 card and still never win a battle.
Or you can take a look at 1000 cards for $28, figure out a strategy, buy the multiples of all those cards needed for under $22 and wipe the battlefield.

Keep in mind I'm building 60 card decks and NOT "Commander".

I've known of Star City Games through my brother and his friends for awhile now and have to say, they've definitely gained they're newest repeat customer.

title: Fun and educational
text:
My 3-year old son received the leapster recently, as well as two games for it. Wolverine and this game. In addition, the leapster includes a pets game. I was reluctant to get him this game because I had glanced at the cartoon and it was garbage. However, the game was bundled with the system.

After playing the pets game i found that it repeatedly asked to be connected to the internet and disliked it. The wolverine game was extremely violent and the actual educational aspect of it was dilluted by all the slashing.

When I reluctantly put in the Penguins of Madagascar game I was surprised to see how often the educational parts interrupted the penguin as he moved about the level karate-chopping rats. So far, the "violence" seems to be limited to animals which youd want your kids to avoid under normal circumstances (rats, cockroaches, giant crocodiles, ect.)

The game features a variety of puzzles such as counting wires to pick the right amount, which square has the most pins, (1,2,3,_) , and placing blocks where their outlines are. My favorite game so far is one where you are given 4 animal pictures and you tap them as you are given clues (which one lives in the ocean?) . I was surprised at how well my son did these games with little help.

In summary, the violence in this game is slight when compared to other explorer games geared towards boys, or video games for the wii or other consoles. The little karate-chopping that is included is overshadowed by the amount of educational games included. Lastly, the game is great for the younger players who cant add or subtract yet.

title: THIS WILL BE A FUN SUMMER TOY FOR MY GRANDSON!
text:
I ordered this as a birthday present for my 3-year-old grandson. I was a little hesitant, because many of the reviews had commented on how flimsy the hinges were. So before starting to put this together, I decided to buy replacement hinges that would be heavier-duty. Well, no luck there! Because the holes were all pre-drilled, and the little hinge had to fit on the end of the 1 X 2 brace, there just weren't any hinges available that would have worked. So the day we were going to start putting it together, we spent half the day running around looking for hinges, but in the end, we decided we would just use the hardware it came with.

I was so pleased at how easy this sandbox was to assemble. My daughter and I (and believe me, we are not DIYers) had it completely assembled in a couple of hours. It was easy cheesy! All the holes lined up exactly right, and it was easy to screw the screws into the right place. I say that, and normally I am the queen of stripping screws, so I was VERY pleased.

The sandbox seems sturdy, and the boards are nice and smooth, so no worries about splinters in little legs.

We finished it off by "painting" a water-seal product all over it. As soon as that dries completely, we are going to staple a landscaping black cloth stuff (what is that stuff called???) to the bottom so that water drains through. The box says it will hold 750 pounds of sand. We did find a sale on playground sand, so we bought six 50-pound bags, which I think will be enough, but if it's not, we can always go back and buy a couple more bags.

The benches, when closed to form the lid, seem to be heavy enough that they won't blow open in a storm. All in all this seems like a great product.

This can be used with the multisensory techniques that are recommended to help kids with dyslexics.  To spell cat, for example, we use the cow, apple, and turtle.  We practice adding and taking away bean bags to spell other words.  We transfer what we learn with the bean bags to our magnetic letters.  I can see an improvement in her spelling from using the kit.

title: Wow - this game is tons of magical Disney fun!!!
text:
We are a Disney family, and I just had to buy this game, even though I thought 19.99 sounded like a lot of money for a board game. We played it twice tonight with our 6 and 4 year olds.

The game is engrossing and really fun for both adults and kids. I agree that it is probably best suited for families who have some affinity for the Magic Kingdom and have perhaps visited the park. We thought it was a lot of fun running all over the park and going to our favorite attractions. My son loved taking the railroad to quickly get from one side of the park to the other. At 6, he had no trouble understanding or playing this game - he won it, in fact.

Our 4 year old was confused and I had to sort of team up and play as her partner. But that's okay. I think this is a fun game that our kids can grow into and enjoy for years. I was impressed with the neat 3-D buildings that attach to the board. My only complaint is that I can see the attraction cards getting worn and bent over time as they are handled. There's really no preventing this. We'll just have to be careful. Overall - we loved it!

title: An Evil Game
text:
This is really an evil coop game that gets harder as it progresses. You think you are doing great, successfully battling the forces of darkness, and then you get slammed by an eruption of evil minions or tainted crystals and the game is over.

My family has played this game four times now, and won twice and lost twice. It is not an easy game to beat, which is good in a coop game. It is well designed with straightforward rules. Plus it is hard not to like any game where you battle a large plastic dragon.

There are a couple cons to the game. While players need to work together to battle generals, I think coop games are more fun when there is more interaction. Shadows Over Camelot is one of the best in this regard. Also, the layout of the board could be better. We spend a lot of time looking for locations where we need to move our heroes. Finally, some of the rules are a bit ambiguous, but that is OK -- you can interpret them to make the game easier or harder.

title: Perfect little dice!
text:
These are, quite simply, some of the prettiest dice I own, and they're also the cutest. The numbers are painted with the color of the dice in mind--all except the white and blue dice have white numbers, while the white and blue have black--and they come in individual tubes so they're kept separate. Each tube has the name of their color on them ("Mini Icy Track", etc) and the tubes all came together in a bag. I took out a D20 immediately and gave it a dozen or so rolls and it seemed to be pretty well balanced despite its tiny size!

These dice are going to be perfect if you're a nerd like me who likes to have a set in their pocket for fidgeting with or just to have on hand, or for a tabletop player who doesn't want their bag to be cluttered when they go to their game sessions--I can't relate to that, because I'm a total dice goblin. ;) They'd also make a cute / funny gift for your players or DM or any random dice-collecting goblin you might know of. These are definitely going to travel to my local Ren Faire with me; I'm sure they'll be good for a laugh!

title: SO different from Sasha
text:
I am a toy collector, I've reviewed the puppy/kitty/etc. surprise line extensively, so please check out my other reviews for more information. This review will cover how substantial the differences between Sasha and Autumn are.

I knew that, as a variant collector, I would be buying Sasha, even though the pictures I could find show her to be similar but slightly different from Autumn, who I also own. I've discovered they are EXTREMELY different and I'm SO glad I bought them both, if you are also a collector, I strongly recommend adding both to your collection.

I'm SO GLAD I picked up Sasha, I just stumbled on her at my local TRU, $24.99, same I paid for Autumn. I go to stores often to check what they have out of the Etc. Surprise line in case I stumble on one I don't have.

Advice from an adult collector; if you find one you're looking for at retail price point IMMEDIATELY BUY IT, there are so many of these that I have literally only seen once, the time I bought them, and didn't see again. There are a couple that are more common that you'll see a lot of, but this whole line moves fast and steeply inclines in price the second it hits the secondhand market, so if there's one specific one you feel you MUST have for your collection, you might get stuck paying upwards of $100 or more for it if you are lucky enough to see it retail and you don't act immediately, and you end up having to resort to the secondhand market. I saw Autumn twice, the first I bought her, and then probably a year later I saw her again. I saw 3 Sasha's at the store yesterday, and one I bought. (I also saw 1 Jilly and 1 Breezy, I followed my own advice and bought them.)

Another issue with buying these secondhand is that you have no guarantee that they have not been tampered with. The amount/type of babies you receive may have been changed, because the babies go for a steep price secondhand even alone.

In all of my pics, Sasha and Sasha's babies are on the left, Autumn and Autumn's babies are on the right. The most immediate difference you see is their face paint. Autumn was part of wave 2, many years ago, and there have been lots of release seasons since then, but it shows, Autumn's face looks SO primitive compared to Sasha. There are 3 times the amount of different paint colors of Sasha's face as there are on Autumn's face. That is an indication of how many passes the painting equipment had to make. More passes, more paint, more time, more money. But they knew, by the time they designed Sasha, that they could make enough units to cover the additional manufacturing cost of Sasha, because the line so far has been a tremendous success.

Sasha has glitter eyeshadow and glitter on her nose, she has more detailed eyes, the faces are much different than I expected, but as I kept looking, I just kept finding more and more.

Sasha only has a bow on her head. Autumn has two bows on her head and her tail, both bows are a ribbon bow and a glitter lace bow, so that's 4 bows on Autumn to Sasha's 1. Autumn's collar and tag are pink, Sasha's are purple. Autumns tail is sewn on to point downwards, Sasha's is a different shape and sewn to point upwards. Both Autumn and her babies contain more stuffing than Sasha and her babies. One of Sasha's babies makes noise (the one in front of Sasha on the far right of her three babies in the photo).

And look at the BABIES! Autumn's babies contain more stuffing and the bows are on the backs of their heads. Sasha's baby's bows are at an angle, they are tilted to the baby's left side. One of Sasha's has glitter ears, none of Autumn's babies (even any I don't have) are going to have glitter on them anywhere. One of Sasha's babies has a black painted nose and mouth, all the rest of the babies are pink nosed. But look at their EYES. Autumn' babies have green eyes with long lashes, Sasha's have blue eyes that are wider opened. Their eye shapes are SO DIFFERENT. The baby's body fabric is matte on Autumn's, but shiny and a completely different fabric on Sasha's.

I hope I've helped you decide whether to add both to your collection and/or which you would prefer to have. Initially there was just the question of whether Rosie or Sunshine were different from one another (they are), but now there are several of these that are slightly different, Sasha and Autumn are not slightly different, they are VERY different. For more basic information please see my other reviews (click on my name), also if you have any questions about any of these, just drop me a comment, I own most of them.

text: This figure is amazing. Whether you plan to display this figure inside or outside of the box or just play with it, this figure is the one to get!! Hasbro did a really good job designing this figure so almost nothing hinders the articulation. His head is a bit hard to move because of the small rubber cape and hood but it doesn't really bother me. His knees are double jointed and he has an ankle swivel which I really love. As for the look, Hasbro did an amazing job. I really love the blend between the rubber and cloth and I was glad that they went with a cloth robe to allow easy articulation. His light saber is connected to the two side-guards so it is a little different from how it is in the movie but that's because you are able to remove the light saber part to display him with the hilt only. The hilt has a great paint job and I love it. Very detailed overall. This figure is great and it is a must have for any Star Wars collector/fan.

I thought I was a intermediate level nerd and thought about building a quad but I don’t want to deal with the software and radio setup. This quad is good for beginners such as myself. I would like to build a quad someday but for now this suits me just fine. My only advice is buy extra batteries. My flight time was about 5 minutes and that was taking it easy. I got little more time with some larger 2200 mah batteries but they just barely fit to the point that the battery cover had to be left off. Really a great experience with my first real quad. I recommend and would buy again based on quality ease of use and fun factor. There’s also a couple sticker sheets to customize the quad.

I've got crafters for kids. You know the kind - kids who wake up asking for popsicle sticks before the sun is even up. I ordered these to save for a rainy day, and today was that day. I handed my 5&7 year old daughters these a few hours ago, and they are still in crafter heaven, giggling and running around with their creations.

We're not new to dotters (or "dot markers"). We go through all craft supplies, dotters included. Here's what you need to know.

- COLORS: strange but wonderful selection. Gold, silver, red, teal, pink, blue, yellow, and purple. No orange, no green, no black, and the colors are quite pastel yet bright.
- QUALITY: great. Easy to use, consistent dots, doesn't flood the paper like other brands.
- GLITTER: Meh. It's there, but it isn't the shimmery goodness promised by the box. My kids don't care. They love it.
- LIDS: A lil chokable. Keep em away from littles
- SHOULD YOU BUY EM? - I would. I did. and I would again.

:) Happy crafting!

title: Great game! Can't wait for expansions!
text:
Fun game! We've been playing this for the past few weeks at least twice a week. The game itself can be fairly challenging and very strategic or fairly straight forward depending on the combination of decks you choose to use. Depending on the five out of eight family decks chosen play is normally between 40 minutes and 2 hours. We will sometimes add a couple additional Epochs (rounds) of play to a game just to ensure we can use more potential of the cards.

The cards themselves have a nice weight and feel to them. The columns (used to 'buy' cards and quests) are nice sturdy wood, with the addition of Greek lettered stickers to assist anyone who is colorblind in playing the game; these letters are also on each card. The other pieces are cardboard cutouts but still sturdy. The box itself offers places for storing everything, including each of the 8 family decks of cards separately. The instructions are pretty self-explanatory and easy to follow. Once you understand what the various symbols are on each card, gameplay will progress quickly. The game also comes with a detailed card description book, in case anyone has any question about a card's actions or abilities.

title: It's really quite perfect
text: It is hard to give a review of it. They have done a spectacular job of catching the feel of Firefly. The pieces are high quality, the art is excellent, the quotes on everything really bring the Joss Whedon flavor to the game. It honestly feels like a perfect adaption of Firefly. They could not have done a better job of translating the show into a game. Highest score possible. As a game, it is very straight forward and interesting, but it is not very involving between the players. It feels less like a competitive game and more like a puzzle you are putting together while you chat with friends around the table. Which is honestly great. If I had to sacrifce anything about the game to make it feel different, I wouldn't. It honestly feels like you are a captain getting crew and flying around the 'verse doing jobs. And money is tight and having spare parts for your mechanic, and getting paid are all very, very important. And missions can go bad as you fly. It's really quite perfect.

The only down side is that it doesn't have an analemma.  (The figure eight in the Pacific Ocean). The analemma shows the latitude of the sun and how much it is ahead or behind mean solar time.  These are really nice to investigate while examining a globe.  (It may be a consolation that the analemma was not included on any of the globes that I looked at before my purchase.) title: WARNING - it burst, fine sand everywhere
text:
I was excited to see if my nephew, who often responds well to sensory toys, would enjoy this banana. We didn't get an opportunity to see, thank God.

My other nephew, and the adults had fun stretching it and rolling it back to shape. We really stretched it. It was fun.

In less than an hour of play, the green rubbed off on our hands, and it became sticky, discolored and wouldn't roll back to shape.

Then it burst when my six-year-old nephew threw it on the floor. The fine sand was not easy to clean up.

I'm glad it burst during his play and not with the intended recipient because you see, my other nephew has Downs and a breathing trach.

This could've been a horrible ending!!!!!

I think you need to make sure your package warnings are clearer, strongly worded. You actively market these as stretch toys for autism, for children in need of sensory play.
Some will put this toy in the mouth. Wouldn't that be awful if it burst into the throat?!

Folks need to know it can burst as it did with us in less than 1 hour.

title: Great Trucks but the "Transformer" is a strange addition
text:
I want to start out by saying that we love the trucks themselves. The wheels are made well and the friction mechanism has enough power to move the trucks a good distance on our carpet floors which is not very normal in our experience with vehicles so far.
The transformer part does leave a lot to be desired. First, the packaging gave no directions for how to "transform" the trucks so you have to find the correct part of the truck to push in for the transformation. Second, the transformer portion is really just a face painted onto the inside of the truck. I think it would have been better suited to just have the inside of the truck present rather than a random face mixed with a truck "body" that doesn't really look like anything.

title: Highly recommended, but DO NOT OVERINFLATE!
text:
Amazing how this super fun ball stays inflated over many weeks of rough play (indoors)!

I imagine that most of the unsatisfied customers likely inflated the ball to the recommended “limit,“ which is ok if you only plan to toss or gently kick back and forth.

For kids who may also like to squish and roll over the ball, I’d recommend filling only to 60% in order to prevent it from popping. This makes it far more durable.

If the ball is tackled upon a sharp twig or stone, for example, it’s understandable how that might result in a puncture or tear.

When inflated to about 60-70% full, this balloon ball is like a Wubble bubble ball that doesn’t need to be repeatedly reinflated (and it’s less expensive)!

Enjoy!

*careful not to pierce the ball while inserting the straw to inflate..with one of the balls that I bought, it took me a while to get the straw fully inserted.

title: and I'm pretty disappointed as they both broke pretty quickly
text:
I bought two of these for my son for Christmas from a local retailer, for indoor use, and I'm pretty disappointed as they both broke pretty quickly.

Out of the box:
Both worked. Turn radius is small, and equal on both, so I assume this is how it is designed. Strangely, the wheels turn further manually than with the remote. The tires have good grip, but are also seem sort of flimsy. I also think that the cars turn over quickly, but maybe that's because my son likes to run them along walls and into things. I have not had a lot of RC cars, but it seems that these things burn through batteries pretty quickly, and after not too much use of new batteries, the range of the controller significantly diminishes and you have to follow it around to use.

However... Within an hour or so of use for one of them, I noticed that when driving it 'straight' it actually turns slightly to the left, and because of this, turning right barely worked and turning left was a super left. Under the car is a plastic adjustment that helps align the wheels, so I put that back to center. Drove the car straight forward and it was straight, but as soon as we turned either direction, you hear an audible click in the car and then the problem resumes. I could have glued the adjustment down, but after less than a day of play I would expect a lot more. As for the second car, after a few more hours of play the steering wouldn't work at all. You could hear gears move in the front of the vehicle, but something obviously had broken. Returning to the store and will invest more money for a better one.

title: The weave approves.
text:
These dice arrive in an understated black case that seems too simple for the artistry that it contains. As soon as you take the lid off, the dice (Red & Blue) catch the light and practically glow. They bring to mind pictures of deep space nebulas or the subtle stir of silt in shallow ocean water. In your hand, these sheer edged dice feel at home. As an avid collector of dice, I am always seeking dice to use for certain characters or NPC’s that I can break out for additional personality with these unique interactions. These dice scream ‘magic user’ to me, with the way they gleam and glitter when thrown and the deep hues of the resin flash between red and blue like fire and ice.

In use, they have served me well. They are light enough that rolling across a tabletop or battle mat doesn’t leave behind dents or dings. In a dice tray they roll reliably and don’t slide much or end up tucked into a corner on a half-face. They do feel surprisingly light in your hand, but this does not detract from the handfeel or the satisfaction of rolling them. For someone on the fence because of the lack of a name brand, you have to see these dice in person, I have yet to see a picture that did them true justice. They are just that beautiful. Easy to read too at a glance, even better than some of my metal dice sets.

As a shameless dice-goblin, I would be delighted to receive these as a gift and would happily order more because the price is fair for what I feel is a pretty awesome product. Highly recommended for any TTRPG player or polyhedral dice addict.

title: Great art, brain burner.
text:
The designer of this game produced another of my all-time favorites, Istanbul. That alone sells me on this one, and it won't take the extra bonuses of the incredible artwork or the cool concept (steampunk time travel) to get me into it.

As far as the gameplay goes, this is much more complicated that most other Kosmos games. It's worker placement, but like Tokaido, once you jump ahead in the game, you can't go back to a space earlier in time. This is a great mechanism that isn't used often enough. Of course, that makes this game more of a brain burning Euro than you'd expect if you've played Istanbul, a game that, while complicated, is actually not that hard once you've played a few turns. In Steam Time, there are considerable consequences to making a single bad move.

That said, if you're into that kind of game, and you can handle a 90 minute playtime, this game is very strong. It won't hit the table as often as some of the slightly less brainy and often shorter games that I own, but that's OK. This game is good, and that's what matters.

title: My detailed physical review
text:
The first thing is that the boards are SMALL. They measure eight inches by eight inches with each square being just a hare short of one inch. There is a five inch clearance in between each board. The frame is sturdy, but can bend if enough pressure is applied.

The boards are made of rigid, but relatively thin plastic. Almost like Plexiglas. They're clear without coloration and they are printed with alternating black and clear squares. Each one fits into the frame with a single screw that goes into the board's center into a tapped hole. Once it's screwed in, the screw will be fairly level with the board surface.
When screwing the screws in, you will need a Phillips head screwdriver with a very short handle as the clearance is only about five inches. You also want to make absolute sure that the board is aligned properly when you screw it in because the black squares are printed on the underside and the ink will scratch and flake off easily if it spins and scratches against the metal frame. It's rather easy to scratch.

Once complete and set up, I noticed a problem. The Chess pieces that come with this set are slightly too big for the board and their bases tend to overlap into other squares. They're also a little bit too tall and easy to knock over. I would suggest getting ahold of some really small Chess pieces to use with this set. Pieces from those tiny portable sets would do. That's what I substituted. If you don't want the plastic bottoms scratching the playing surface, you can even glue a piece of felt or cork under each piece. To give it a little weight, you might even fill the pieces with some lead shot before covering the bottom.
If you have access to really tiny wooden pieces, all the better. And nothing is to prevent you from making this thing into a sci-fi Chess set. It certainly looks the part. I'm sure there's some amazing Chess piece ideas one can come up with for this that will fit the board. Generally, for this set, the shorter and smaller based the pieces are, the better.

The only other suggestion I have for playing this game is to put something light and brightly colored underneath the board. Even a piece of paper will do. I have it on a dark stained wood table and seeing the black squares on the bottom board is virtually impossible.

Despite any negativity, once built, the set looks slick and nice, albeit small. It would make for an excellent conversation piece. or decoration.
This product could be greatly improved with the inclusion of either slightly larger boards with larger squares or smaller Chess pieces that fit the squares or at least ones where their bases don't overlap into other squares. Having a light solid color for the white squares on the bottom instead of having them clear and see through for the bottom board would be an improvement for playing on a dark colored tabletop.

I would suggest grabbing the rules for "Millennium Chess", which is a free set of rules for playing three level Chess, and using them for this set. Those rules are much more concise and better put together than the rules included with Stato Chess.

title: Finally a properly metallic looking C3PO, and they included the silver leg!
text:
Yet another great kit from Bandai, my wife got it for me which put a huge smile on my face.

Putting it together was about as easy as the other Bandai Star Wars models in my collection so far with the only exception being some incredibly tiny pieces on the head, chest, sides, hips and legs which could easily be lost or broken if you aren't careful with them, I actually recommend gluing them into place carefully so they don't fall off later. It includes some great detail pieces like an alternate chest piece with a restraining bolt on it, an alternate face with a dent in the forehead, a comlink that one of the hands can hold, and an alternate set of arms that have some movement, but the pistons in the elbow area won't be shiny like the rest of the model and are actually the same color as old mustard gold C3PO toys we all grew up with. The decals look better behind the knees and in the tummy section, especially when combined with Mr. Mark Softer decal setter.

A tip for making the eyes look better would be to use black panel liner paint and a small wire that will fit in the hole behind the lenses. Dip the wire in the black panel liner paint and then carefully fill the holes in the lenses with the black paint and let it dry, any excess can be taken off later with paint thinner and a qtip. Another tip would be to paint the gold details on his palms instead of using the stickers or decals as they end up just looking flat.

Definitely a worthy addition to any Star Wars fan's collection.

title: Fun Play for Toddlers; Fairly Easy Assembly for Adults
text:
I assembled this in an hour, which was longer than I expected but really not too bad. I am fairly handy & I had very few issues.

This does require your own phillips head screwdriver. An allen wrench is provided in the hardware package.

Speaking of the hardware package: I loved it! KidKraft sorted out the hardware into sections in one blister-style package with cardboard backing that was labeled and easy to see from both the front and the back which items were which (Screw A, for example). I have never had hardware for a DIY assembly project come like that, and it made it so much easier!

The instructions were easy to understand, entirely done in graphics (no written instructions). Pay attention to details on which way holes, painted elements, and sides should be facing, and you shouldn't have any trouble.

Unfortunately, I had one glaring problem right away with the very first step in the instructions: there were NO holes in the panel that the screws were supposed to go into in this step. After a few minutes of rechecking that I really had it right, and that I wasn't confused about which side I was using, I confirmed that the holes really were missing! Now, thankfully, I was able to skip that step, and began assembly with the next step, and so forth, and discovered that as the other panels were secured into place, the missing holes were compensated for. By the end, the whole thing held solidly together even though those two (nonexistent) holes & screws were not used.

I had very little other issue, other than a couple of screws near the end that didn't line up perfectly with the holes, but I managed to get them by shifting the wood around a little.

As to the playtime elements of this kitchen, it is so cute and creative! There are great elements that my 10month old granddaughter loves! It's just the right height for her to pull up on. As she grows, I know we're going to want to add more play dishes & food, but for now it's great as is. I do wish there was a way for the ears/oven mitts to stay put, like velcro perhaps, so they didn't fall off so easily. Otherwise, we love this kitchen and have lots of fun playing with it!

title: Phones interfere w/controls, goes berzerk
text:
Drone flies perfectly without a phone connected to it. However, once a phone is connected you enter the casino where bets are taken to see where it goes and how it acts. Sometimes it flies and sometimes it goes crazy. Not anything I'm willing to risk injury or damage for.

If you're lucky, you may just lose control and the drone will just hover. On a bad roll of the dice not only does it lose control but it actively goes crazy and flies in any direction, fast.

The remedy is to disconnect the wifi immediately... however this is not practical if you want to use this for photos. So it's basically unuseable.

Tried with 4 different phones: Google, Samsung, and two different Apple phones. Different pilots. All the proper calibration... It is definitely the phone interfering with the controls, likely at the controller end but could be the drone accepting interference too.

title: Terribly made and should cost much less!
text:
I already knew this was a cheaper knockoff of the barbie glam pool, but I had much higher expectations for what I was buying...

I'll start with the pros, since there's ONLY 2. The pool is a pretty good size, and its easy to put together. Which is the only reason it has 2 stars instead of 1.

It's a good thing it's easy to put together tho, because there are no instructions and you have to just figure it out by looking at the picture on the box. And altho the pool is big, there's no support on the sides. The only hard thing in it for support is a bendy plastic piece you thread around the top, and because it's vinyl, it's easy to poke a hole in while you're doing that. I wouldn't recommend using this without having 5 towels under it and a cookie sheet or pie pan to hold it. Because you also can't pick it up to dump the water out without something to hold it flat since it's unsupported. But if you're going to mess with all that, save your money and just go buy a pie pan and use THAT as your barbie pool. I guarantee it's of equal value (if not higher quality....) to this piece of garbage.

Also, it was super dirty right out of the box. There was dirt literally caked onto the plastic. I'm not sure what that's about. And to demonstrate just how thin and cheap the plastic is, there was jagged plastic (from it not being stamped all the way out of the mold or whatever it is during the process of making it) all over many of the pieces that I had to cut off before I gave it to my 5yr old so she didn't hurt herself.

This should be like $5-$8 at the most. I don't recommend this at all.

title: AMAZING FOR MY SON AT RESTAURANT!
text:
I recently purchased the Baby Grip Rattle Toy and have been extremely impressed with its functionality and design. The product serves as both a highchair rattle and a portable hand rattle, making it a versatile and convenient tool for both mothers and babies. The strong suction base easily attaches to high chairs, tables, trays, floors, or any smooth surfaces, making it a great feeding helper for mothers. The red heart button on the base also allows for easy separation of the baby grip rattle toy, making it portable for on-the-go play.

One of the standout features of this toy is its ability to promote fine motor skills in babies. The different parts of the toy can be spun, pressed, and twisted, helping to strengthen fingers dexterity, hand-eye coordination, and counting skills. The product is made of safe and odorless ABS material, which is safe for babies to play with. The round polishing, fine skin soft technology also ensures that the toy is gentle on a baby's small hands.

I highly recommend this product as a warm gift choice for newborns, first gifts, and Christening gifts for 6-12 month old toddlers or 1-3 year old toddlers. The safety material and multi-functional creative design make it a great choice for any parent looking for a safe and versatile baby toy.

Parental Tip: Bring this along to restaurants and since it has a suction cup, you can directly attach this to the table and that will keep the kiddo distracted and/or focus!

title: IMPRESSIVE PERFORMANCE & GREAT VALUE!
text:
This car is so impressive! I looks great, it is FAST and agile. I moves around on pavement/smooth surfaces at a speed that surprised me. Acceleration is extremely fast! The 4 wheel drive really holds this car to the ground especially while turning and while giving it full power from a dead stop. It moves around in the grass/dirt or off smooth surfaces like a jack rabbit and is still very controllable - I haven't had this much fun with one of these since I was a small kid. It comes out of the box ready to run, just charge the battery up first.

My list of things that make this car fun and a great value:
1. There is knob on the remote to turn down the top speed so that you can get used to it without a major crash or slow it down in bumpy areas. This lets you give it all the throttle without loosing control.
2. Comes with 2 batteries that lasted me around 20 ~ 25 minutes average each depending on how hard I drove it.
3. This car It is made so that it can be taken apart to replace/fix any parts that could break in a major crash. This make this a 'hobby grade' car in my opinion, instead of a toy that breaks leaving you trying to find a way to fix it.
4. The car comes with some replacement parts and tools so that you can get right back to fun if you were to break something. This car is very sturdy, however accidents happen - I'm impressed that they put the thought behind the decision to include these most common parts and tools to replace them.
5. The user manual is well written in English and has great pictures and diagrams. This is a big deal for me as my experience with many products these days is poorly written documentation.
6. The is a COMPLETE parts breakdown with part numbers in the user manual. This is a first for me with a ready to run RC car or truck.

I'm 100% satisfied with this car. At this price point it just doesn't have a down side.

text:
Our family really enjoyed working this Lego ice cream puzzle. It took us three weeks of working on it a few minutes now and then. I love that it could be worked in sections by color. There was just the right level of challenge without being frustrating for my elementary-aged kids.

We noticed after working the puzzle that several colors of ice cream are the exact same photo but with the colors edited to appear different. Just an interesting observation.

I would give it 5 stars for how much we enjoyed this puzzle, but I have to take a star off for the quality. The pieces are all the same basic shape. When trying a piece to see if it fits, it would get stuck and then its cardboard layers would peel apart slightly when the piece was tugged free of the wrong space. This puzzle also had the worst amount of puzzle dust I have ever seen. I emptied the box of cardboard dust 4 separate times as we sorted through pieces. And then it left a scattering of puzzle dust all over the table after we put the puzzle away.

Overall, we really enjoyed this puzzle and I'm sure we will assemble it again in the future.

You can almost buy a Hubsan quad for this price! Heck the camera version of Hubsan X4 is only $60, $50 without.. That is.. UNLESS IT IS PRIME WITH A LIGHTNING DEAL!

I am starting to see the pattern.. Introduce "Prime" service.. Keep the prices low for a year or so.. Then slowly start jacking up the price so that the stupid customers don't know that the benefits of the service are nothing more than a premium that is paid for membership like Costco or Sams. And of course I am seeing this price jack thievery AFTER they raise the price of Prime and let that settle in.. More money for Prime? no problem, after all it's a great service.. Keep inching up the prices without fear because we know those dumb customers are so addicted to watching Teen Wolf for the 5000th time that they won't even notice.

Thanks Amazon.

title: Buy these, you wont regret it - unless you hate fun.
text:
Best "Stock" darts I have seen. I bought these for my 8 year old nephew. We have him over maybe once a month and he is obsessed with nerf. The actual nerf darts are CRAP compared to these. These fly very straight and precise, at MAYBE the cost of range but frankly... so much more accurate that the added "range" you get from a lighter nerf dart, doesnt even matter since your accuracy is utter garbage at that added range, so it really doesnt compare AT ALL.

These are heavier and as a result fly very "true" to the target and even hurt a tad more than normal nerf darts. I have been shot in the eye a few times (yes, I should wear protection) and while it stings, it wasnt too bad.

ONLY reason these get 4 stars is the glue seems pretty crappy. I bought some Gorilla Glue and have re-glued about 20 of the 100 heads and now they are ROCK SOLID darts. So just be prepared for that. After a week or two, the heads will be coming loose, buy some Gorilla Glue, rip off, and re-glue the heads and youll never have to worry about them again. MUCH MUCH higher quality and performance than standard "Nerf" darts.

Will buy these again when needed.

title: "Sings" Shouldn't Be The Only Word In Quotation Marks
text: This Barbie does not "sing" two "songs," she "sings" the chorus of two songs, already named by previous reviews. I actually had to look the lyrics to the second chorus up because I swear I thought the word "spark" was "fart." That should say something about the quality of the audio, as well. I, too, can't stand that there's no volume control or "off" switch. I did not know you could get her darn skirt off at all (I'm pretty sure the box says you can't), and her flip-around hair is SO creepy. They've also stuffed her gown with paper to make it appear fuller in the package. The box says the doll cannot stand up on her own, but that's not the case. My 3.5-year-old has balanced her to stand a couple of times. What's infuriating is that she cannot sit. Not only do her knees not bend, her waist doesn't bend, either. She also cannot put her microphone down, so I guess as a Princess she's continually making public speeches? If you can stand the annoyance of listening to the same two 20-second-long audio clips ad nauseam, by all means, get this as your child's FIRST Barbie. That way, they have no expectation of how a Barbie is supposed to move or that you should be able to change her clothing.

title: Planet Putty Slime
text:
[[VIDEOID:daf46808bf7ac22bd3da6a72820567d]] The Planet Putty Earth Series by Universal Specialties is a cute fun item for kids. What kid does not like slime? None that is who! The slime comes in three round containers they each have a planet they represent on them. The colors are bright and fun. The slime is not sticky and will not stick to your furniture or floor and it does not stain anything either. This is always a plus. The slime can be stretched or squished and molded into forms. The slime often makes funny sounds when squishing it from the air bubbles that get trapped in the slime when playing with it. Then when you are done just place it back in its airtight container for storage. This is a classic fun item for kids.

title: Regular pencils will never be good enough after these!
text:
Love, love, LOVE these!

Scent- We received the 5 scents shown. I was concerned about my kids' hands smelling like the fragrance oils but am happy to say this doesn't happen. We've had them for about a month and used them every day, they still smell great. We do keep them in their cute plastic pencil tubes between uses, and the cartoon toppers make it easy to pick specific ones out as desired.

* Sugar Plum - Lightly fruity but mostly perfume-y, doesn't really smell like plum
* Candy Cane - Bright, fresh minty scent
* Holiday Cheer - Linen-fragrance fabric softener fragrance with hints of mint and cinnamon
* Gingerbread - Spicy gingerbread with a hint of black pepper
* Hot Cinnamon - Smells exactly like Red Hots, very cinnamon-y and sharp (my favorite out of this Smencils collection)

Pencil - Very good quality! Naked wood barrel, there's no coating on it which is unusual, but very smooth and not slivery at all. It's cool to know that it's made out of recycled newspapers. It sharpens beautifully, and the lead makes a nice, strong dark line that erases well. The eraser is also great.

All in all, we're addicted. We bought the Halloween pack and had to have the rest of them, including this one and the regular pack. The kids have fun choosing which one they want to use. :)

title: Don't be fooled by pictures...
text:
Always being somewhat fascinated by the look of the Earth from outer space I thought this globe was a pretty unique idea. Unfortunately, the marketing imagery differs so much from what you actually get it's pretty startling. I had assumed there would be small, individual beams of light emanating from the globe, almost like pinholes. Instead, the printing on the globe simply allows for some areas of the map to shine brighter than others when the device is plugged in. Further still, the globe is so thin you can see shadows of the inner-workings of the motor moving around on the surface all the time.

If it weren't for the price I might be a little bit more generous with the stars but this was a very disappointing purchase.

title: Travel edition changes make it much less fun.
text:
I love Blokus Duo. Its much more practical and fast paced than regular Blokus. You can easily play round after round and get into rapid, elegant competition.

This travel addition, though, is a huge step back in execution and aesthetics.

The snapping element of the pieces is a huge slowdown and just feels clunky. Visually, it also makes your strategy harder to focus on.

The travel compartment is tedious to pack and comes apart easily.

I think they would have done much better to make a magnetized version of the game. As it is, the elegance of Blokus disappears along with a lot of the fun.

After trying repeatedly to use this version, on the go. I eventually just retired it and carried the full sized box around.

When I lost my full box copy, despite it being my all time favorite game, I didn't even bother pulling this one back out.
